#1635. Deportivo La Coruna vs Barcelona - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:25, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:29

Barcelona will bid to post a sixth straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna at Estadio Riazor on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan giants have won four of their last five matches against Deportivo, including a famous 8-0 success in the corresponding game during the 2015-16 campaign.

Deportivo boast a record of three wins, six draws and four defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 15 points leaving them in 12th position in the La Liga table.

The Blue and Whites finished second in last season's Segunda Division table to secure a return to the top flight, and their opening to this campaign has certainly been positive.

Antonio Hidalgo's side will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 defeat to Alaves, but they have picked up four points from their last three games at this level, including a 2-1 success over Osasuna in their last game in front of their own fans on November 2.

Deportivo have picked up nine points from their six home league matches this season, and their last success over Barcelona did come in front of their own fans - a 2-1 win in March 2017.

These two teams have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is Barcelona that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to Deportivo's 22, while 20 of their encounters have finished all square.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League, with the result leaving Hansi Flick's side in fourth spot in the overall table on 12 points.

While the Catalan giants are in an excellent position to secure a spot in the knockout round of the Champions League, they also sit at the top of the La Liga table, picking up 36 points from their 13 matches courtesy of a record of 12 wins and one defeat.

Barcelona are three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid and five clear of third-placed Atletico Madrid, and they posted a 3-2 success over Villarreal in their last league fixture.

The Blaugrana have the best home record in La Liga this season, picking up 18 points from seven matches, while they are comfortably the highest goalscorers in Spain's top flight during the 2026-27 campaign, finding the back of the net on 51 occasions.

Barcelona now have three straight league matches against Deportivo, Atletico Madrid and Celta Vigo before resuming their Champions League campaign against Manchester City on December 8.

Deportivo La Coruna form (all competitions):

Deportivo's squad is in strong shape at the moment in terms of availability, although Bright Ede (hamstring) and Zakaria Eddahchouri (wrist) remain major doubts for the home side.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has scored five times in La Liga this season and is set to continue through the middle despite the fact that he is three games without a goal since returning from a knee injury at the start of November.

Mariano Soriano and Luismi Cruz have both scored twice for Deportivo this season, meanwhile, and the pair are set to continue in the starting side.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal was absent against Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday due to a minor ankle injury, but the Spain international is set to return to the starting side for this weekend's contest.

There will be no Fermin Lopez, though, following the attacker's red card against Villarreal last time out; Roony Bardghji (knee) and Xavi Espart (ankle) are also definitely out of the clash.

However, Rodri and Andreas Christensen both have chances of being back in the squad.

The ankle injury that Alejandro Balde suffered against Sabah is not serious, meanwhile, so the left-back could potentially make the squad.

Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Joao Cancelo, Dani Olmo and Raphinha could also all be brought into the starting team following the European clash with Sabah.

Deportivo La Coruna possible starting lineup:

Roman; Navarro, Noubi, Loureiro, Quagliata; Luismi, Soriano, Casado, Rodriguez, Hernandez; Aubameyang

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Olmo, Gordon; Raphinha

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey is the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical issues, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

And ignoring the fact that Klopp does not generally delve deeply into the scouting process, hence the transfer committee is likely to be just as influential as it was during Brendan Rodgersai??i?? tenure (if not more).

The good news is that Jurgen Klopp seems far from keen to jump onto the transfer bandwagon. Heai??i??s instead decided to focus on the rich pool of players already on the teamai??i??s rolls, either on loan to other clubs or playing for the youth club. This greatly reflects his vision and ability to curb any impulse to seek a ready-made answer in the transfer market.

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

In the last two weeks, Klopp has recalled loanees Tiago Ilori (Aston Villa), Sheyi Ojo (Wolverhampton), Ryan Kent (Coventry City), Danny Ward (Aberdeen) and Kevin Stewart (Swindon Town). Against Exeter City, he also utilized all of these players barring Ward, and played youngsters Cameron Brannagan, Joao Carlos Teixeira, Jerome Sinclair, Brad Smith and Connor Randall.

This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1630. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1629. Valencia vs Osasuna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 09:32, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 09:35

Valencia will aim to post a third straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign at home to Osasuna on Sunday afternoon.

Los Che comfortably lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 46 wins to Osasuna's 21, while 25 of their 92 matches have finished all square.

Valencia boast a record of three wins, three draws and seven defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

It has been a tricky first third of the league season for Valencia, but there have been signs of life in recent weeks, having won two of their last three in the league and three of their last four in all competitions.

Javier Aguirre's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano in La Liga, while they also beat Tavernes 6-0 in the Copa del Rey on November 10.

Valencia, who finished ninth in Spain's top flight last season, actually have the second-worst home record in La Liga this season, securing only two points from seven league games in front of their own supporters.

Los Che are also the joint-second lowest goalscorers in La Liga this term with nine, and that is a concerning record heading towards the winter break in Spain's top flight.

As for Osasuna, a record of four wins, three draws and six defeats from 13 matches has brought them 15 points, which is enough for 13th spot at this stage of proceedings.

Jagoba Arrasate's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Malaga, but they did lose their last away fixture - a 2-1 reverse to Deportivo La Coruna on November 2.

Los Rojillos have struggled on their travels this season, claiming only three points from six matches, suffering five defeats in the process.

Osasuna lost 1-0 to Valencia in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign, and they have only managed to win one of the last five games between the two sides.

That said, Osasuna do have a recent away success against Valencia to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory at Mestalla in August 2023.

Valencia will welcome Jose Gaya back into their squad this weekend following a suspension, but Sergi Canos, Diego Lopez and Jesus Vazquez are again expected to miss the contest.

Arnaut Danjuma is likely to return to the squad, with the attacker not involved against Rayo Vallecano last time out following the death of his father.

Gaya for Pablo Maffeo could be the only change from the team's last match given the impressive nature of both the performance and the result.

As for Osasuna, Alejandro Catena is out of the game through suspension, with the 32-year-old sent off in the team's home success over Malaga last time out.

Jorge Herrando was back on the bench against Malaga after recovering from an injury and could now be introduced into the starting team here.

Ante Budimir has scored nine times in 13 league appearances this season, and the Croatian will once again lead the Osasuna line in this contest.

However, Abel Bretones, Aitor Fernandez and Rockson Yeboah are still injured.

Dimitrievski; Martinez, Tarrega, Copete, Gaya; Raba, Pepelu, Rodriguez, Rioja; Guerra, Sadiq

Herrera; Rosier, Herrando, Boyomo, Rico; Moncayola, Gomez; Ruben Garcia, Oroz, Barja; Budimir

Valencia have struggled at home this season, while Osasuna have found it difficult on their travels, so we are finding it tough to back either to win with any real confidence.

A stalemate could be on the cards at Mestalla.

Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

It’s the incisive, between-the-lines passes that Arsenal are currently lacking. Perhaps a bit of rustiness after such a long break between games?

Calafiori drives past Bogle and whips over a cross that is behind Havertz who has to backpedal to head it which robs his effort of power. Trafford drops to his knees to gather.

Rice takes an unnecessary touch instead of playing a first-time through ball to Madueke and Leeds recover to attack up the left. Okafor’s cross sails way too long and Bogle cannot keep it in.

Lewis-Skelly holds off Stach but then throws up his arms as if flapping a cape and clocks Stach in the face. Leeds are awarded a free-kick.

Excellent hold-up play by Calvert-Lewin is ruined by a shoddy Amapadu pass. Arsenal move it out to the right where Leeds enmesh White in the offside trap again. The crowd howls in frustration.

Someone seems to be banging a drum. Is this Selhurst Park? Okafor is penalised for grabbing Konsa’s shirt as he tried to spin the centre-back on halfway. Arsenal switch it to their left and Calafiori crashes into the box to cross. The ball deflects through the area and over the penalty spot but there’s no runner to meet it.

As TNT Sports points out, Leeds are trying to press Arsenal high but the positioning of Rice and Lewis-Skelly is much better than it was at Brighton.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal have been eager to play quick passes over the Leeds defence in these opening exchanges. Arteta’s side usually prefer to build up more slowly but they are looking for Havertz quite early. A consequence, perhaps, of Leeds pushing quite high up the pitch.

Okafor’s blistering 20-yard shot is deflected behind for a corner. The linesman’s flag was up because he said Calvert-Lewin had moved towards the ball in an offside position but the referee overrules him.

Arsenal defend the cross solidly but Bogle is covering diligently when they try to play Madueke clear with a long ball.

Now Madueke is caught offside on the left after a Muharemovic mistake threatened to let Havertz burst through before he laid it off instead.

Justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Aresnal launch a counter up the right and the telepathy between White and Saka for once breaks down when White runs offside for a return pass. Elvedi was there to sweep up in any case.

Muharemovic reads the game well and snuffs out a long pass looking for Havertz, shifts the ball up to Calvert-Lewin who is grabbed round the waist by Gabriel and Leeds are awarded a free-kick in the centre-circle.

Saka, miles offside, takes on a cross that he should have headed with a leaping volley instead and Trafford saves at very close range. Slick work between Odegaard and Madueke to get the ball to Saka.

Both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Leeds kick off, attacking from right to left, going all the way back to Trafford standing outside his box and he clips a long pass up the right and Leeds are immediately penalised with the linesman’s flag.

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea says it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

The most interesting aspect of that Arsenal lineup, I think, is the inclusion of Noni Madueke. It seems like he’ll be on the left flank, as the replacement for the injured Christos Tzolis. Madueke has played a handful of games on the left since joining Arsenal from Chelsea but it hasn’t happened nearly as frequently as had been expected when he first arrived. A left-footer on the left wing: old-school!

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1626. Alguacil looks at Milan’s favouritism, respect and playing to win: “Life or death match”

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

For Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

“What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

“We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

“We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”

“Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

“Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

“He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”

#1625. Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he said: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

'I think Manchester United are currently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville said in August. 'Would you agree?'

Carragher said that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

#1624. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1623. Real Sociedad vs Sevilla - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 10:13, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:16

Two teams enjoying solid campaigns in Spain's top flight thus far will lock horns on Sunday evening, as Real Sociedad welcome Sevilla to Anoeta Stadium.

Real Sociedad just about lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 55 victories to Sevilla's 52, while 35 of their 142 fixtures have finished level.

Real Sociedad will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Europa League, with the result leaving them down in 27th spot in the overall table and out of the knockout round playoffs at this stage of proceedings.

It has been a struggle for Real Sociedad in Europe this season, and they were also beaten 3-2 by Racing de Santander in Spain's top flight last weekend, so the Basque team will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions on Sunday night.

La Real have had a strong campaign in Spain's top flight, with a record of seven wins, one draw and five defeats from 13 matches bringing them 22 points, which is enough for fifth spot in the La Liga table.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side now have three straight league games against Sevilla, Real Madrid and Villarreal before returning to European action at home to Torreense on December 10.

Real Sociedad have been strong at home in the league this season, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat, picking up 13 points from six matches.

Sevilla have won five, drawn four and lost four of their 13 league matches this season, with 19 points leaving them in sixth spot in the table, three points behind fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

The Red and Whites are without a win in their last three La Liga fixtures, though, losing at Getafe at the start of the month before drawing back-to-back games with Alaves and Real Betis.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only actually won one of their last seven league matches, but sitting sixth after 13 games represents a solid start to the campaign.

Sevilla recorded a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad when the two teams last locked horns in May 2026, but the corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 success for the Basque outfit.

Los Nervionenses have picked up eight points from their six away league matches during the 2026-27 campaign courtesy of a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Real Sociedad currently have a number of injury issues, with Yangel Herrera, Alvaro Odriozola, Ander Barrenetxea, Jon Aramburu and Lander Astiazaran on the sidelines.

Head coach Matarazzo will make changes to the side that started against Palace in the Europa League, with Carlos Soler, Orri Oskarsson, Igor Zubeldia, Sergio Gomez and Luka Sucic among those set to return to the team for this match.

Mikel Oyarzabal has only scored three times this season, but the Spain international will continue in the final third of the field for the Basque outfit.

Sevilla will once again be without the services of Marcao, Jose Angel Carmona, Alfon Gonzalez and Miguel Sierra on Sunday due to injury problems.

However, the visitors did not suffer any fresh issues against Real Betis last time out, and given the strength of the performance, it could be a case of same again in terms of team selection.

Isaac Romero and Robbie Ure are both pushing to be included in the final third of the field, but the expectation is that Lucas Stassin will again be given the nod in that area.

Remiro; Fort, Zubeldia, Sarr, Gomez; Sucic, Gorrotxategi, Soler, Guedes; Oyarzabal, Oskarsson

Vlachodimos; Iglesias Sanchez, Castrin, Salas, Suazo; Agoume, Guridi; Vargas, Fofana, Correia; Stassin

Real Sociedad will be aiming to bounce back from a European defeat in this match, and home advantage could see the Basque team shade a close game.

#1621. Manchester United Plan 20 Million Pound Bid For Bundesliga Defender

Home » Home 2 » Manchester United Plan 20 Million Pound Bid For Bundesliga Defender

Louis van Gaal’s hand may be forced into making a transfer this January, after injury woes continue to adversely effect the Red Devils. And it looks like he’s set to raid none other than the Bundesliga club that dumped them out of the UEFA Champions League.

23-year-old fullback Ricardo Rodriguez has caught the eye of the Manchester United officials, with The Sun reporting that the club have sent scouts to watch him twice already and that he is very high on manager Louis van Gaal’s transfer wish list.

The Swiss defender is valued int he region of 20 million pounds, but has a release clause of 27 million pounds at German club Vfl Wolfsburg, where he has spent the past 4 years. This means that Manchester United will have to negotiate quite a bit to land the player without breaking the bank yet again. They will also have to be wary of Real Madrid, who are also reportedly interested.

Italian right back Matteo Darmian came off with an injury in the second half of United’s 1-0 loss to Southampton, he is the latest in the list of injured defenders at the club. Phil Jones, Ashley Young, Luke Shaw, Marcos Rojo and Antonio Valencia are all members of the walking wounded at Old Trafford.

This means that buying a fullback is a top priority for the club this January and we could well see a bug bid launched by the Red Devils for the highly rated Rodriguez.

#1620. Swansea City vs Cardiff City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 10:19

Swansea City square off against Welsh rivals Cardiff City on Sunday looking to remain in the top eight of the Championship table.

Meanwhile, the Bluebirds make the journey across South Wales sitting nine points adrift of their hosts.

With Freyr Alexandersson still deliberating over whether he intends to leave Rosenborg and if that move may be delayed until December, Ashley Williams will remain as interim boss for this game.

The Swansea legend has only accumulated one point from games against West Bromwich Albion and Middlesbrough, yet his side came from behind to earn a share of the spoils versus the Baggies and pushed leaders Boro all the way at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night.

Those 2-2 and 1-2 scorelines versus the fifth and first-placed teams in the division suggest that Williams has had a positive effect on the group after Vitor Matos's surprise switch to Strasbourg.

Nevertheless, this remains a Swansea outfit that have lost five of their last seven Championship fixtures, their only success being a 4-0 victory at home to Blackburn Rovers.

Despite that drop off in form, Swansea remain just eight points off top spot, emphasising that a win in this contest will keep them in contention with the teams above them ahead of Alexandersson's potential arrival.

As for Cardiff, they are reeling from the shock 4-0 defeat at home to struggling Preston North End in midweek.

Not only did the Bluebirds lose their eight-match unbeaten record at the Cardiff City Stadium, they have now conceded 11 goals across their last three home contests.

Brian Barry-Murphy's side now sit just six points above the relegation zone at a time when they are still searching for their first away success since earning promotion back to the second tier.

However, it should be noted that their last two away games have been at Wolverhampton Wanderers and Norwich City, two of three teams in the division that have collected 16 points across their last six matches.

Cardiff travel to Swansea having failed to win any of their last four games at the Swansea.com Stadium, losing three times without scoring before a 1-1 draw on their most recent visit in August 2024.

Having served a one-match ban, Swansea left-back Josh Tymon will return to the starting lineup.

However, Marko Stamenic is still absent through suspension, while Goncalo Franco and Ronald are expected to remain on the sidelines.

Jay Fulton and Zan Vipotnik are pushing for recalls in midfield and attack respectively.

With several defenders sidelined, including Perry Ng who is still having a knee injury assessed, Barry-Murphy may not make any changes to his Cardiff backline.

Nevertheless, David Turnbull, Joel Colwill and Chris Willock are all in contention for returns in midfield and the final third.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Welsh, Cabango, Tymon; Just, Fulton, Eustaquio; Opoku, Vipotnik, Eom

Trott; Kpakio, Fish, Bielik, Bagan; Robertson; Tanner, Moylan, R Colwill, Willock; Salech

While Cardiff are expected to deliver a response to their capitulation to Preston, we cannot ignore that Swansea have been competitive against top teams under Williams's short tenure. Therefore, the Swans get our backing in this fixture, albeit with a winning goal potentially coming during the closing stages.

#1619. Europa League preview: Olympiacos vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan will make the trip to Greece with the hopes of turning a corner against Olympiacos after a rough start to their Europa League campaign.

It has been a tale of two competitions this season so far for Milan. In Serie A they are inside the top four and have won eight games out of 12, leading to suggestions of a Scudetto bid. However, in Europe they have lost three of four, and sit in the bottom eight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It means that they’ll have to be perfect to even be in with a chance of a top eight finish – given you’ve needed at least 15 points in the last two seasons. Nevertheless, a point and gaining a bit of momentum across all competitions would still be appreciated.

Game date: Thursday, November 26 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: Karaiskakis Stadium Referee: Chris Kavanagh (VAR: Bankes)

As mentioned, things have been going quite well for Milan domestically. Sunday’s 5-1 victory against surprise package Frosinone was another example of the potential of this team, but there remains a necessity to find some consistency.

This is especially the case when it comes to the Europa League, in which the Rossoneri have been quire frankly awful. A 4-0 win against RB Salzburg in round two was the only glimmer of light, with the other three games being defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring.

As things stand right now, Milan would not even make the play-off spots as they sit outside the top 24. There is only one point in it and even eighth is only four points away, though the runway is getting shorter with only 12 points to play for.

The result of this is that Amorim is expected to name quite a strong side for the game, but we must start with the injury absences. The big doubt is Strahinja Pavlovic, who needs another check on a kidney stone problem despite playing 20 minutes off the bench against Frosinone.

Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano and Ruben Loftus-Cheek have all missed the past few games due to various issues and will not be available on Thursday either.

On Tuesday, the news broke that Milan will be without Luka Modric, who felt a tweak in his right thigh during the last game. The Croatian will be given Thursday night to recover and potentially the Cagliari game too, with the hopes of having him back at the start of December. Then, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi have already been ruled out.

The other bit of news is that Fikayo Tomori returned to training on Wednesday, which is a big boost given how thin the options are in defence, but it remains to be seen if the Englishman is deemed fit enough to play a part after his absence.

With the squad running quite thin, Amorim won’t have many options to rotate, nor does he have the luxury to with the standings.

Nevertheless, there will be one at the back, where Pervis Estupinan is expected to start. Mike Maignan starts behind Sankhoun Diawara and Koni De Winter, with Mario Gila at right-back again.

Modric’s injury means Ardon Jashari will be given a chance on Thursday, and it’s one he must take. Alongside him, he’ll be covered with reliability from Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot, which should help.

Finally, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are expected to start on the flanks, with Goncalo Ramos through the middle.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Torriani, F. Terracciano, M. Cissé, Tomori, Perera, Comotto, Vos, Ossola, Hutchinson, Cisse, Menon

Injuries & suspensions: Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Modric, Pavlovic, Camarda, Bartesaghi

Olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

The spending was almost totally offset by four big sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

In the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey may be the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical issues, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

AC Milan and Olympiacos have faced each other four times. Two came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19, which means that the meetings were almost 60 years apart.

In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

The most recent encounters were eight years ago as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

Starting in midfield, the obvious choice here is Ardon Jashari. This has been called his game by the Italian media and it’s tough to disagree. If he’s going to have a future with the club beyond this season, a strong start tomorrow is imperative.

The other obvious choice is Pervis Estupinan. The Ecuadorian is a late entry into the expected XI, despite reports linking him with a potential exit in January. Bartesaghi’s injury means he’ll be given a chance and maybe, just maybe, it’s not too late for him. Something of promise needs to be seen, though.

With Milan lacking Modric in their midfield, it could allow someone like Remo Freuler to take the game by his pace. He’s got plenty of European experience and with the Rossoneri likely to rely on Jashari to set the pace, he may take the edge.

Then, if Leon Bailey starts, he’ll be the big threat of the night. Facing Estupinan and Diawara, he’ll have the opportunity to face a duo that have no relation yet. If he catches them out, it could be a long night for the Diavolo.

It’s been a real case of Jekyll and Hyde for Milan in the Europa League, to the point where it’s tough to call which side we’ll see. Logically, after such a heavy win at the weekend, the visitors should be coming away with three points.

However, both teams aren’t brilliant defensively and it could become an open game as a result. Considering what’s at stake, though, the Rossoneri may just edge past the hosts, but it won’t be easy…

#1618. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1617. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1616. Fulham vs. Bournemouth - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 10:39, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:43

Unbeaten in five Premier League matches, Fulham welcome in-form Bournemouth to Craven Cottage for Sunday's matchweek 12 encounter.

While Alvaro Arbeloa's team have struggled for goals during their unbeaten run, the Cherries recorded a 10th consecutive victory on Thursday, with five of those wins coming in the top flight.

After a slow start to life under Arbeloa, Fulham have gradually found their feet under the former Real Madrid boss.

The Cottagers began the 2026-27 season by collecting just two points from a possible 18, although their four opening defeats were all narrow, but the capital club have since turned their form around.

Fulham have collected nine points from an available 15, making the West Londoners one of the division's form sides ahead of this weekend's fixtures.

However, the 15th-placed side remain hampered by two issues: their attacking inefficiency and inability to protect leads, highlighted by Arbeloa's men scoring exactly once in seven consecutive matches and dropping 10 points from winning positions.

Only Brentford (11) have surrendered more points after taking the lead, and addressing both weaknesses could determine whether the improving Cottagers remain in the bottom half or challenge for a top-half finish or European qualification.

Bournemouth, though, have no such concerns heading into Sunday, with Marco Rose's men flying high domestically and in Europe.

Thursday's victory over Celta Vigo preserved their perfect record atop the Europa League standings after five rounds of the eight-match league phase, while their domestic turnaround since a 5-1 hammering at Stamford Bridge has been striking.

After failing to keep a clean sheet in their opening six league matches under the new manager, the Cherries have shut out four of their next five opponents, with a maximum return of 15 points propelling them to fifth in the Premier League table.

While Bournemouth cannot overtake fourth-placed Liverpool this matchweek, they could strengthen their grip on fifth if the teams below them stumble.

Having watched their side win five of the last eight top-flight meetings with Fulham, the travelling supporters will hope for another positive result against the London club to secure a sixth consecutive league victory and an 11th across all competitions.

The hosts' improvement under their Spanish boss, however, suggests that the Dorset-based visitors will encounter stern resistance at Craven Cottage, adding to the intrigue surrounding this weekend's contest.

Fulham have a relatively healthy squad, although Emile Smith Rowe (hip) faces a late assessment before Sunday, Joachim Andersen is likely to miss out and Benjamin Lecomte (Achilles) is sidelined for the season.

Joshua King is the only Fulham player to have scored more than once, with his two goals complemented by strikes from Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Cesar Palacios, Gonzalo Garcia, Oscar Bobb and Ryan Sessegnon.

Bournemouth, meanwhile, owe much of their league position to Evanilson and Marcus Tavernier, whose combined 11 goals account for 61% of their 18 top-flight strikes in 2026-27.

Six-goal Evanilson has also demonstrated his creative threat, registering four assists in 11 appearances, two more than Justin Kluivert.

Like Fulham, the visitors have most of their squad available, although Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) and Alex Toth (thigh) are absent; Julian Araujo faces a late assessment as he targets a return from a thigh problem, while Junior Kroupi will be checked after falling ill before Thursday's comeback victory over Celta.

Leno; Tete, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Muniz

Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Christie; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Fulham's five-match unbeaten run suggests that Bournemouth should expect resistance, but their habit of surrendering leads remains a concern against opponents brimming with confidence.

With Evanilson and Tavernier providing a consistent scoring threat, the Cherries have our backing to exploit the hosts' game-management problems and secure an 11th consecutive victory across all competitions.

#1614. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.
