#1572. Fat margins

Thanks to Lewis for taking care of the blog yesterday as I was unable to watch the Borussia Dortmund match live. I saw that we’d scored early but only saw the final score well after the full-time whistle, so I guess it was a little disappointing not to have built on that fantastic hit from Viktor Gyokeres.

I think while I have some frustrations overall with our inability to turn dominance into goals, I’m more comfortable with it when we’re actually making chances. I think the manager would have a far bigger issue on his hands if we weren’t, and on Tuesday night the fact we had 30 attempts on goal tells you the problem isn’t chance creation, it’s about being clinical.

It wasn’t that long ago that it was the other way around. We found it hard to make goalscoring opportunities and for me that’s much more of a worry. It doesn’t mean we can’t improve, it doesn’t mean January becomes any less important the closer it gets, it’s just that the solution lies with the players we have who should be capable of better. There were a couple of other opportunities for Gyokeres that could easily have made this a better night for him and for Arsenal, Declan Rice hit the post, fine margins that shouldn’t be impossible to squeeze in our favour. Make ’em wider, thicker.

In the end though, I think the bottom line is quality of personnel. Over the last few seasons the only front three player we’ve had who looked like he could become top, top quality was Bukayo Saka. He was certainly on that trajectory until injuries became a real hindrance, and we saw that this season there were modifications made to his game to make him more effective. I know the discourse around him was a little polarised, but I saw a player more involved, who looked sharper and capable of producing the kind of volume that made him so impactful.

Saka isn’t one of those who finishes every chance he gets, he’s a guy who just keeps going until he makes something happen. The hamstring injury, and then the ongoing Achilles issue made it harder for him to contribute, but I really was encouraged by his season until the injury he sustained against Bayern. And it’s interesting to me that while it might be the kind of player he is anyway, we’ve basically asked Noni Madueke to replicate ‘Old Saka’ in terms of that kind of volume of shots and crosses. He’s had 11 shots across the last two games, and perhaps a single goal from those appear to be a scant return, I think it’s how we need him to play and how Arsenal can maximise what we’ve got up front.

There was an interesting comment on the Arses yesterday wondering how it is that Mikel Arteta can coach and improve defenders and midfielders so well, but not do the same with his attacking players. Some will say it’s because he’s a coach who is defensively minded and this is his wheelhouse. This is what he’s good at. Make a great defence, build a solid midfield in front of them. Perhaps there’s an element of truth in that, but for me it’s down to the players he has to work with.

If the raw ingredients are good, the recipe has a much better chance of being good, regardless of the talent of the chef. If you get to work with players like Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard etc, all of whom arrived in at a relatively young age (Rice perhaps the exception because he had a lot of experience, but Arteta has still made him better), you can develop that potential, build relationships, and see that come to fruition on the pitch.

Up front though, I don’t think we’ve had that level of talent. What can you do with a Willian or a Marquinhos? What can you do with a Gabriel Jesus whose knee explodes (perhaps as we saw in those opening few months before injury hit, you could have done a lot more)? Was Gabriel Martinelli’s plateau down to Arteta’s coaching or the player’s ceiling? I think the fact he’s playing now in Saudi Arabia says a bit about that. I think Arteta squeezed a lot out of someone like Leandro Trossard, who arrived at 28 and became a better player than he was at Brighton, but ultimately there are limits. The same goes for our two strikers, Gyokeres and Kai Havertz. On their days, they can get you goals, but there are too many days when they won’t, and I don’t really think it’s a coaching issue.

We also need to remember that there was a season when Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal scored more goals than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004. It’s not as if his coaching, per se, is an impediment to scoring goals – but like anything it’s layered and multi-factored. We had to become more defensive when all of our attackers were basically banjaxed, we still managed to finish second that season when all we had on the bench was a end-stage Raheem Sterling. If that has tipped the balance a little too far the other way, then you can understand it, and Arsenal are the masters of the single-goal margin victory these days.

I think we can do more to score more, I think some of the players we have are capable of delivering more goals and assists, and over the next few months – being realistic about what we might do in January – that’s what we need to lean into. But my gut feeling is that until such time as we have better attackers to work with, this will remain an issue – and it’s worth saying that said issue is one we still find a way to achieve success with more often than that.

I’d just like some fat margins once in a while.

#1571. Inzaghi recalls beating Liverpool in Athens and ’emotional’ affection from Milan fans

In the hearts and minds of AC Milan fans around the world, Pippo Inzaghi’s name is inseparably linked to Athens.

Inzaghi gave Milan their seventh Champions League title on 23 May 2007 in the Greek capital with a brace that swept Liverpool aside. The first goal was an Andrea Pirlo free-kick that he deflected in, the second an assist from Kaka that he rounded Pepe Reina from and slotted in.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was he who allowed the Rossoneri to take their long-awaited and long-desired revenge on the Reds after the Istanbul defeat two years earlier. That feat – at the Spyros Louis Olympic Stadium and not at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium – has remained in the minds of all Milan fans.

It is the most recent of the Champions League titles raised to the sky, and while Inzaghi’s mind is on finishing the job with Palermo (top of Serie B), he will watch his old side on TV tonight. The former striker spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Dor you and for Milan, thinking back to Athens is never trivial…

“Absolutely. In Athens I experienced one of the most important nights of my career, so it’s a city I associate with special memories and that’s why it will always remain close to my heart.”

Tell us three memories from that game. Let’s start with a pre-match one…

“The anticipation of the match: I knew how important that final was and I felt it could be a special evening.”

“The highlight was, of course, the second goal. A moment later, I realised the cup was really close.”

“After that final, I didn’t sleep for ten days. I woke up in the middle of the night thinking that victory with my goals had been a dream.”

Given what that cup represented, that is, the famous ‘after Istanbul, there’s always Athens’ that was printed on the back of AC Milan’s second shirt this season, is the 2006-07 Champions League a joy comparable to Italy’s World Cup victory in Berlin a few months earlier?

“They’re two different memories because they’ve both enriched my footballing life. Winning the World Cup is the ultimate accolade for any footballer.

“Athens, however, also had a special meaning for Milan’s history: we were coming off a disappointment that I’d experienced from the outside, from the stands [he was injured] and I could finally be on the pitch to contribute to the victory.

“Fate gave me a second chance, and it went as you all know… However, I wouldn’t rank the two nights of glory because I carry them with me in different ways.”

Before Milan-Atalanta, when you came to San Siro, you understood from the huge applause and chants how much the Rossoneri fans still love you and you said: “Every time I come back here it’s like it’s the first time.”

“Returning to San Siro and feeling that affection was truly emotional for me, especially because it was the first time for my son Edoardo, who is now five years old.”

What does it mean to you, years after leaving AC Milan as a player and the 2014-15 season in which you were the coach, to still be so loved by the fans?

“I spent extraordinary years at Milan: the bond with the fans was born from goals, victories, but also from the commitment I always tried to put in. Knowing that all this has gone down in history is a priceless gift.”

What do you hope for Milan on their return to Athens tonight, needing a win given their position in the Europa League table?

“I hope we can face the match with character and return home having experienced a great European night. I know how much that shirt means and how much the fans expect from a match like this. I hope the team can give them joy and a victory.”

#1570. Calvin Bassey: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa sends "no chance" transfer message to Man United

By Ben Sully | 27 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:52

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out a January move for Manchester United-linked Calvin Bassey.

Man United currently have the Premier League's second-worst defensive record after shipping 23 goals in 11 games.

As a result, the Red Devils are widely expected to bolster their backline when the transfer window opens for business in the new year.

Bassey is among those who have been mentioned as a potential target, having established himself as an accomplished Premier League centre-back during his time with Fulham.

However, Arbeloa has dampened Man United's hopes of a January swoop, insisting the focus is on agreeing a new contract with Bassey rather than entertaining the prospect of a winter sale.

“I’m so happy with Calvin and obviously he is not on sale," Arbeloa told reporters ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash against Bournemouth.

"No chance he can leave this club in January and I think he is happy here. He is one of our captains, he is one of our leaders.

"It is normal that so many clubs are interested in him, it is good for him and good for us. It means he is performing really well.

"We are working on a new contract, and I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bassey's current contract is set to expire at the end of the season, although Fulham hold the option to trigger a 12-month extension.

Speaking about last weekend's draw with Manchester City, Bassey said: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

"I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations."

Bassey has started all 11 of Fulham's Premier League games this season and has formed a strong central defensive partnership with summer signing David Affengruber.

The pair have helped Fulham build a five-game unbeaten league run in which they have conceded no more than one goal in any of the five matches.

#1568. How Arsenal are evolving their build-up play

Arsenal have evolved how they attack this season. I think there have been quite a few improvements in the way Arsenal seek to create danger that haven’t necessarily shown up on the score board so far. This is an especially sensitive subject this week after draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund- games where Arsenal took deserved one goal leads but failed to build on them.

However, the failure to add true ceiling raising talent in attack this summer- despite heavy interest in Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez- has led to Mikel Arteta needing to coach his way out of a tight spot. The manager has made some alterations to his materials to make Arsenal’s final third play less austere this season. Here are some ways Arteta has evolved the team’s approach play.

Rotations and fluidity Under Mikel Arteta we are accustomed to seeing the left-back enjoy a role based on improvisation and freedom. Last season, we began to see Jurrien Timber take up some very advanced roles from right-back. This stands to reason because full-backs are not typically assigned a marker by the opposition, so it’s easier for full-backs to pop up hither and thither in advanced areas without detection.

That license has been extended this season. Let’s look at some examples just from the Newcastle game. David Raya launches a long pass here and *squints* who is that playing the role of target man and bringing the long ball down at centre-forward? By God THAT’S EBERECHI EZE’S MUSIC?!

And look who that is sprinting up beside him in the number 10 position but right-back Jurrien Timber. Madueke has a shot and hits the post from this build-up. Look at where Timber is when Madueke takes the shot.

Then we see Odegaard at left-centre-back here (sure, what the hell?) and whose buccaneering forward run is that he is picking out?

Why it’s Riccardo Calafiori. Spotting where Jurrien Timber is when Arsenal have shots on goal has become a favourite pastime of mine. Where’s Jurrien in this shot?

Here he is running down the left-wing to tee Havertz up for a shot.

This is how the move starts for the Eze goal. Konsa at right-back, Timber at centre-back, Calafiori in central midfield.

When Konsa clips the ball forwards, Madueke has shown for the ball centrally like a number 9 while Havertz has pulled into Madueke’s position. Calafiori continues his run like a horse trotting along without a jockey. You get the message by now, Madueke’s goal in the second half sees Timber make a pass to Havertz in left central midfield.

One of Arsenal’s first shots of the season is created by Tzolis drifting over to the right wing and we had seen Saka manipulated into all sorts of shooting positions prior to his injury. Tzolis was also frustratingly caught offside at St. James’ Park when he had drifted over to the right wing. Hincapie spent a lot of time in central midfield against Borussia Dortmund. Arsenal are a far more fluid outfit this season.

This sense of shapeshifting is reflected in midfield. Rice and Odegaard pretty much always start, the identity of the third midfielder can be any one of Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Zubimendi and Merino, all of whom are high level players with very different qualities. Just the identity of those names gives you face value options.

Declan Rice leads the Premier League for assists this season and all of them have been from open play. That alone tells you something different is happening. Roles in midfield are less defined. There were probably times last season when the Rice and Zubimendi combination became a little too ‘side to side’ and not cutting enough. Spending lots of money on 28-year-old Bruno tells you what Arteta felt his midfield was missing last season- risk and thrust.

Bruno expanded on this in the pre-Dortmund press conference, he spoke about the midfield at Arsenal being far less defined positionally, where Rice, Odegaard and AN Other (usually Bruno) will freelance between the 6, 8 and 10 positions. ‘It’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

‘If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.’ I expanded on midfield a little more in my column from two weeks ago.

Arsenal have not been able to land a genuinely elite attacker in what feels like years now. Fortunately, Arsenal have a manager who might be the best in the trade at this moment in time. As well as moving to a more freestyle approach all over the pitch, there have been signs of improvement in individuals.

Firstly, Noni Madueke seems to be thriving on the opportunities afforded him by Saka’s recent injury. He looks more confident, his actions have greater clarity and Arsenal have treated Madueke as if he is Saka, that is to say, they give him the ball at every opportunity and rely on Noni’s capacity for repetition.

He is averaging 3.28 shots per 90 in the Premier League this season compared to 1.85 per 90 last season. (He is also averaging fewer crosses per 90 this season which implies an increasing willingness to vary his play and drive at goal as often as he does the by-line). His pass completion rate has jumped by 10% on last season.

The goal against Dortmund saw Madueke cushion a long pass, kill it perfectly and shift it to Gyokeres, who turns and lashes the ball home from 25 yards. That is not a goal description I could have envisaged in September. Gyokeres started the season very badly indeed.

Lewis touched on Gyokeres’ increased creativity this season during the international break. It looks to me as though there has been a focus on him being allowed to offload the ball after one or two touches. You don’t really want the ball getting bogged down with Gyokeres, the more touches he requires the more his technical limitations will show.

Gyokeres gets the ball from a Raya kick here and Madueke is nice and close to him and running in behind.

It means Gyokeres can take one touch and then play in behind. We see something very similar for the chance he creates for Havertz away at Brighton, Havertz is already moving when the ball comes to Gyokeres and it means he can take one touch and hook it in behind.

Then there is his lovely one-touch assist for Declan Rice in Munich where, again, he has a runner very close to him and it allows him to play the ball first time.

Arsenal have also been working on getting Eze in behind and through on goal, look at his position here when Odegaard plays a through ball in Munich.

And look at where he is when he slots Havertz’s lovely slide-rule pass at St. James’ Park.

Getting Eze in on the shoulder of the opposition right-back is another move we are seeing bear fruit sporadically. This fits into a wider theme I touched on a fortnight ago about Arsenal going in behind more often and more quickly this season.

#1567. Pointless points to play for

There’s not much going on yet, but of course we have a game against Man City on Sunday. Typically this is a fixture which would mean a lot in a season, but this time around, given the pending judgement after their appeal for being found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges, it doesn’t really feel that way.

I see their fixtures and even the latest run of poor results doesn’t connect in the same way it would have done in seasons gone by. I wonder how different it is for the players and the manager. I guess they have to be professional and do the job in front of them. Regardless of what kind of punishment is handed out to City in due course, there are three points to play for on Sunday.

But if they are punished the way they should be, it feels like this game – along with all their other games – just shouldn’t matter. When I wrote about this at the time, I said this was something of an existential issue for the Premier League, and that’s still how I think about it. We have a club who have cheated, lied, obstructed, and damaged the competition itself just going through the motions until such time as they receive a points deduction or an expulsion or a transfer ban or all of those things, and it kind of feels pointless (three points aside etc etc haha).

We still don’t know when that’s going to happen, but if it does come down mid-season, how can we look at this campaign as one which is fair? I suppose that very much applies to many of the seasons in which they actually won the league, because they did it thanks to their cheating, but surely pre-decision games against City and post-decision games are not going to be the same in terms of their competitiveness. That’s a problem, but one I hope doesn’t preclude something happening sooner rather than later because despite how quiet it’s gone around them, this issue hangs over this season’s Premier League like a toxic cloud.

I suppose if there is an upside about this fixture right now, it’s that we no longer have to endure questions about Mikel Arteta and his relationship with Pep Guardiola. He’s scuttled off into retirement, showing his true moral compass by backing City when they were found overwhelmingly guilty despite saying in the past he’d walk away if such a thing were proven. Now we have Arteta versus Enzo Maresca, a man who has already decided his tenure there is likely to be short, so has taken to wearing outfits in order to audition for Guy Ritchie’s new Netflix special about geezers and wide-boys who are gentlemen in country houses who ride horses and love the rough and tumble of the good old days on the streets but wear a monocle while doing the violence and their wife is always called Cassie or something.

Anyway, let’s see what the manager says at his press conference later, which we’ll cover on Arseblog News in the afternoon.

Elsewhere, I know I mentioned it on the Arsecast yesterday, but I wanted to point you in the direction of the Arseblog gift guide, which could take some of the hassle out of your Christmas shopping. There’s Arsenal-related merchandise from all kinds of fantastic independent creators (and some official ones too), and you can find it here – https://gifts.arseblog.com/

A big shout to Andrew Allen for putting this together and compiling it, along with tech help from Tom and our friend @bootifulgame.

Finally for today, I just wanted to provide a little health update. After what feels like an interminable wait, I got results of scans/biopsies yesterday, and the news is that there was nothing more going than they initially thought. So, in context that feels like good news despite the obvious fact the overall diagnosis remains a load of shit I could really do without.

However, I can’t even begin to explain the relief of knowing. Like with anything, the absence of information creates a vacuum, and regardless of how hard you try to stay busy and to distract yourself, your brain tries to fill the gap. I don’t know if my brain is particularly unique, but there were times when that filling in was very, very dark, which becomes increasingly difficult to shake off as the days goes on and you’re waiting and waiting for info.

I now have a date for the first chemo session and everything goes from there. As I said in my initial update about this, I’m going to be around as much as I can be because I need the normality, but if there are some days in December etc when I’m not, that’s probably why. I definitely won’t be on tropical island in a hammock, but maybe that’s something to aim for when all this over.

Again, thank you all so much for your messages, they’ve really helped me over these last few weeks. To know so many people are in my corner, so to speak, has kept me positive when my silly brain went to those places I wish it hadn’t. Anyway, we have clarity now, let’s get on with it!

Right, I’ll leave it there for today. Have a great Friday folks, and for some extra reading, here’s Tim’s column on the evolution of Arsenal’s build-up this season.

#1566. Why Man United could be missing skipper Bruno Fernandes for Premier League showdown with Brentford

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 13:50, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 13:56

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has revealed that captain Bruno Fernandes is a major doubt for Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford due to an illness.

Fernandes was unable to train on Friday, having picked up a virus.

Pochettino has said that no final decision has been made on the Portugal international at this stage of proceedings, but he is a major doubt for the game with the Bees.

"We will not take any risks. We will see when he wakes up tomorrow," Pochettino told reporters during Friday's press conference at Carrington.

There has been criticism of Fernandes' form this season, but he has still come up with eight goals and three assists in 16 appearances for the Red Devils during the 2026-27 campaign.

The 32-year-old scored twice against his former club Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night and had been in line to start against Brentford.

Fernandes now has four goals and one assist in five Champions League appearances this season, in addition to four goals and two assists in 10 Premier League matches.

Man United will also again be missing Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford through injury this weekend, but Luke Shaw returned to the bench against Sporting and could potentially receive some minutes in this contest.

The Red Devils will be going in search of just their second Premier League win of the campaign against Brentford.

A disastrous campaign to date has left the Red Devils in 19th spot in the Premier League table, claiming only eight points from their first 11 games of the season.

"This is a group of players who want to do well, who want to perform. Our job is to build confidence. We arrive full of energy, positive, but it's difficult for the players when the results haven't been up to scratch, but we try to help them as best we can," added Pochettino.

Man United have lost two of their last three Premier League matches against Brentford, but they recorded a 2-1 win over the Bees in the corresponding game earlier this season.

#1565. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. #1563. Roma vs Monza - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 14:05, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 14:08

After an impressive midweek result in Europe, Roma will resume their domestic title challenge when Monza visit Stadio Olimpico on Sunday evening.

Now aiming to maintain pressure on leaders Lazio with a fifth straight Serie A win, the Giallorossi have just halted the reigning European champions.

Staying within two points of league leaders Lazio - also their loathed city rivals - Roma stormed to a 5-1 win at Parma last week, with star striker Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals and substitute wing-back Wesley getting a hat-trick of assists.

The capital club moved ahead of Scudetto holders Inter Milan into second spot, as they reached 36 goals for the Serie A campaign - more than any team at this stage of a season since 1990-91.

Gian Piero Gasperini's side also remain unbeaten in the league, with their last domestic defeat dating back to April, so they were full of confidence before taking one of football’s toughest tests in midweek.

Malen was on target again as Roma fought back for a 2-2 draw with injury-hit Paris Saint-Germain, becoming the first team to stop PSG claiming maximum points in this season’s Champions League.

However, due to calamitous collapses against Real Madrid and Manchester United earlier in the league phase, they are still at risk of an early exit with just three games to go.

Next month, Gasperini’s men will face a crucial double-header in Rome, hosting Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League before taking on old foes Lazio in Serie A.

First, though, Roma must meet another former manager: following a reunion with Luis Enrique, Ivan Juric will bring Monza to the Olimpico.

An old friend and former player of Gasperini, Juric completely failed in a brief spell as Giallorossi boss, and he is still trying to rebuild his career lower down the Serie A table.

His Monza side ended a run of four defeats by beating Fiorentina 3-0 on Monday, keeping a rare clean sheet and lifting themselves out of the relegation zone.

Almost inevitably, Tottenham Hotspur target Gustavo Varela struck either side of half time, taking the prolific striker onto 11 goals from his his first 11 Serie A appearances and further inflating his transfer fee.

However, the Brianzoli have lost four straight away games before Sunday’s clash in the capital, and they have collected just one point away from home since returning to Serie A.

Dating back to their relegation campaign of 2024-25, Monza have lost 17 out of 21 on the road - and their record against Roma is even more grim.

To date, they have lost all three league meetings at the Olimpico by an aggregate score of 8-0, while only taking two points from six games overall.

Both Lorenzo Pellegrini and Devyne Rensch are still unavailable for Roma, but Leonardo Balerdi could recover from an ankle injury in time to make Sunday’s game.

Gasperini is likely to rotate his squad, so after Santiago Castro surprisingly started in Paris, Malen should reclaim his place up front.

With 26 so far, the latter has already equalled the record for Serie A goals scored by a Roma player in one calendar year. That also leaves him just two shy of Marco Van Basten's Dutch record, which was set with AC Milan in 1992.

Meanwhile, Varela is looking to challenge Malen for top spot in the Capocannoniere rankings: his tally of 11 goals is the best for a promoted side at this stage since Gabriel Batistuta back in 1994.

Monza captain Matteo Pessina returned to action on Monday evening, having missed most of the campaign so far, but Michael Folorunsho, Yvan Maye and Cyril Ngonge are all set to sit out.

Svilar; Ghilardi, Ndicka, Hermoso; Lulli, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Dybala, Mora; Malen

Thiam; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Carboni; Birindelli, Akinsanmiro, Pessina, Mangas; Mota, Robinson; Varela

Precedent and present form both suggest Roma will continue their streak of Serie A wins.

The Giallorossi simply cannot stop scoring, while Monza have conceded at a rate above two goals per game.

#1562. Self-serving Scottish clubs were always going to ensure Craig Mulholland's youth football revolution was doomed to failure

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026

Given how quickly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

However, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a new head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those plans have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a new watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those plans might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

But that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

It is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any new proposals.

The SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these plans through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

But nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has provided an update on Carlos Baleba and Marcus Rashford ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Brentford.

#1559. Opinion: Richard Hughes' bargain deal has saved Liverpool's season

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is currently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on new players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has quickly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he quickly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

#1558. Tonali explains his ‘two stories’ with Milan after turning from fan into player

Sandro Tonali has once again revealed his love for AC Milan, and spoke of the emotion of playing for his boyhood team.

Tonali played for Milan from 2020 to 2023, making 130 appearances and scoring seven goals, winning the Scudetto in 2021-22. He moved to Newcastle for €64m in what was a painful exit, given that he was being talked about as a potential future captain.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With the Magpies, the Lodi-born midfielder played 110 games, scoring 10 goals, before moving to Tottenham Hotspur in the last summer window for €108m. There, he has linked up with Roberto De Zerbi, someone who also has Milan in his heart.

There continues to be sporadic rumours about a return to the Rossoneri one day, but given his value it remains a pipe dream for now. Tonali was interviewed by Fútbol Emotion Italia and he recalled some significant moments that he had at Milan, with his comments relayed by Calciomercato.com.

“I have two stories with AC Milan. The first is up until I was 20, when I had never fully embraced the AC Milan world. The second is from 20 onwards for the following three years,” he began.

“I was a fan for a long time. Then when the matches allowed it, maybe there was a game at San Siro when in Serie B we almost always played on Saturdays, we often went to watch. It was something passed down in the family from my father, so I’ve always had it even since I was a child.

“Then past 20 years of age it changed, because as a player you can’t maintain the same relationship with the team that you have as a fan. I did that the first year too, but I felt it too much, so after that I experienced it differently.

“But maybe it was even more beautiful because you put the fan aside and you started to realise that I suddenly found myself there, with the team of my heart and in a stadium like San Siro.

“The first year wasn’t easy, I found myself struggling a bit. But it went well for me also from the point of view of playing without fans. It wasn’t nice, but for me personally as a player at that moment it was good because there was less pressure.

“But all in all it was bad because that year without fans it all seemed like friendlies, it didn’t feel like football. Milan means a lot to me.”

#1557. Man United Confidential: Carrington crash adds to Mauricio Pochettino's woes, as new boss set to cut players' days off... and why the wait goes on for coach Silvia Tuya

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:16 EST, 24 November 2026

As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.

The collision between a vehicle and a cyclist on one of the two approaches to Carrington, where United’s players and staff are regularly seen driving through a security checkpoint, meant it was closed off for several hours on Friday while an ambulance and police cars attended the scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the cyclist was taken to hospital to receive treatment for injuries that were not life-threatening and no arrests were made.

However, anyone leaving Carrington had to take an alternative route in the opposite direction. That included the players after training and Pochettino and his staff following his first pre-match press conference.

The accident on Friday completed an eventful 48 hours at Carrington after a rogue drone operator filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first training session and posted it on YouTube. He later took the video down and apologised for the intrusion, which United sources said was the right thing to do – even though they had not contacted the uploader directly and do not intend to take legal action against him.

They insisted there was not a breach of security at Carrington, but claimed a number of laws had been broken. Insiders promised a robust response to any further incidents to protect the rights of the club and its staff, and warned that those responsible would be ‘exposing themselves to significant legal and financial risk’.

It's been a testing first few days for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United boss

One of the unexpected issues to hamper the Argentine was a drone filming his first training session

Meanwhile, players leaving Carrington last Friday had to take an alternative route after a serious road accident near United's training ground

Confidential understands Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems as soon as possible.

The squad were pictured arriving around 8.30am as they looked to regroup after the 4-0 hammering at Anfield and begin their preparations for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on Wednesday night.

The Argentine is eager to spend as much time as possible with the players on the training ground, having only taken over as United boss last Wednesday – four days before the Liverpool clash.

United now face 11 games in 43 days and sources believe there may not be too many days off as Pochettino tries to haul his team out of the relegation zone and ensure qualification for the knockout stage of the Champions League.

At least the indications are that he will allow the players to stay at home the night before games at Old Trafford, rather than having them cooped up in a hotel like some previous United managers.

Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems

Matheus Cunha won’t play any part against Sporting following his red card in United's last Champions League tie against Roma three weeks ago.

Confidential has learned the Brazilian was set to claim the player of the match award after scoring two late goals in the 3-2 win over Roma, only for UEFA to step in.

UEFA rules prevent a player who has been sent off from receiving the award and so the selector – in this case Steve Cooper, the former Leicester, Nottingham Forest and Swansea boss who is now one of the governing body's technical observers – was forced into a late switch, picking Bruno Fernandes instead.

Cunha’s absence will be keenly felt in Portugal. He played no part in Tuesday’s training session at Carrington, instead working on his own in the gym.

At a time when United have the most porous defence in Europe’s top five leagues and Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven are all struggling for form, Pochettino is going to need Harry Maguire.

Pochettino overlooked the experienced Englishman from the start for the trip to Anfield but ended the match with Maguire on the pitch and he was United’s best defender on another desperate afternoon.

Maguire is walking the tightrope of a ban as he remains on four yellow cards after 11 league games. Players are hit with a one-match ban once they receive five or more yellows prior to the conclusion of the 19th league game of the season – eight matches from now.

Even after Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal, Pochettino can ill-afford to be without Maguire going forward.

Pochettino is going to need the experience of Harry Maguire to hold his defence together but he faces a ban if he is booked again

United are still waiting to see if Pochettino’s strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya can join his staff at Carrington despite hiring new fitness coach Sam Wilson.

Wilson has joined United following his departure from Parma in October, having only moved to the Italian club as head of performance in the summer after 12 years at Arsenal.

It is understood Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team because she is waiting to see if a work permit will be approved.

She joined the US national team staff in October 2024 shortly after Pochettino, and travelled with him, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and analyst Alec Scott when they flew from Cincinnati to Manchester by private jet last week.

Strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team

Some of the early changes under Pochettino have been more subtle than others. Observant fans may have noticed that when the club announced the team to face Liverpool at 3.15pm on Sunday, it was in positional order.

Previously, United’s line-up has been listed numerically, leaving fans to deliberate over the formation. But Pochettino liked to name his team positionally at Tottenham and Chelsea, and admitted in a Q&A on MUTV last week that he wants to do the same at United.

It was clear from the club’s social media post on Sunday that Pochettino would be sticking to the 4-3-2-1 formation favoured by Michael Carrick, with Patrick Dorgu returning on the left wing and Cunha leading the attack.

Not that it lasted very long, as Pochettino admitted he was forced to put his game plan ‘in the bin’ inside eight minutes when Yoro was sent off.

This weekend’s match-up between United and Brentford brings together the most ill-disciplined English team in all competitions and the dirtiest team in the Premier League.

No English team has had more players sent off this season than United’s four – Yoro twice, Cunha against Roma and Martinez against Chelsea.

Meanwhile, Brentford are bottom of the Premier League’s disciplinary 'points table' thanks to their three red cards and 22 yellow cards. So expect referee Rob Jones to be a busy man on Pochettino’s home debut.

Leny Yoro brings down Alexander Isak at Anfield and is sent off - his second red card of the season

Richard Arnold, who preceded Omar Berrada as United's chief executive, pocketed a £5.53m pay-off to stand down after Ineos moved into the club

While Omar Berrada found himself back in the firing line last weekend, the man he succeeded as United’s chief executive was cutting a much more relaxed figure.

Richard Arnold, who led United between February 2022 and December 2023, was spotted enjoying himself on Chester’s popular Eastgate Street on Saturday night – 24 hours before a beleaguered Berrada watched United’s 4-0 thrashing 30 miles down the road at Anfield.

After stepping up to replace Ed Woodward, Arnold was in charge of United for the period spanning United’s strategic review which led to Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquiring 29 per cent of the club. Once it became clear that Ineos would take over the day-to-day running of United, he accepted a £5.53million pay-off to stand down, with the club’s general counsel Patrick Stewart stepping in on an interim basis.

Arnold is now enjoying a quieter life as an executive director at Norton Motorcycles and, it would appear, nights out close to his home near Chester.

It was there that he met a group of United protesters outside his local pub in June 2022 and admitted that the last 12 months had been ‘a f****** nightmare’ and United had ‘f****** burned through cash’. Nothing much seems to have changed since then.

Exactly how much of an option he is this campaign isn't clear but it feels highly unlikely that Liverpool would sign someone to essentially replace him.

Liverpool have been linked with Gustavo Varela, who is currently lighting up Serie A with Monza. He's got 11 goals and an assist in his 11 league matches this season, including a brace against Fiorentina at the weekend.

It's a strange one, though. Liverpool don't necessarily need a striker, given Alexander Isak is the clear first-choice and scoring goals, while Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo can also play there.

Of course, there's also Hugo Ekitike - we do expect the Frenchman will be back this season, even if he's been out long-term. Exactly how much of an option he is this campaign isn't clear but it feels highly unlikely that Liverpool would sign someone to essentially replace him.

Unless they feel a new striker is necessary to compete for trophies this season and the next. And they might. Ekitike is a gamble at this stage.

It certainly appears that the chance to sign Varela will be there. Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that he's available for around €35m, which is potentially a steal if his goal scoring numbers hold up.

Though, Serie A's history is littered with strikers who started a season remarkably well only to fade away gradually, never replicating the form again. So while Varela is playing brilliantly, he'd be an enormous risk.

#1555. Man City injury news: Antoine Semenyo return timeline revealed as Enzo Maresca delivers “good news”

By Oliver Thomas | 27 Nov 2026 14:24

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City attacker Antoine Semenyo.

The 26-year-old has missed each of the last eight matches across all competitions since sustaining a knee injury in City’s 3-2 Premier League win over Ipswich Town on October 17.

Semenyo was initially ruled out for eight weeks by Maresca, with a return in mid-to-late December deemed a realistic target for the Ghana international.

However, Maresca has now suggested that Semenyo could make a first-team comeback for Man City sooner than anticipated.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday ahead of Man City’s trip to Arsenal on Sunday, Maresca said: "We have good news. Semenyo is quite close [to returning]. That is good news for us!

“But the rest, they are all OK... [Semenyo] is already on the pitch, he is very close. Hopefully he can be [back] probably next week. We hope so.”

It remains to be seen whether Semenyo will be back as early as next Wednesday when Man City host Leeds United in the Premier League, but he could instead feature in some capacity away against Brentford on December 5.

Discussing whether Semenyo has been missed, Maresca added: "I was laughing with him yesterday; I told him that in the Premier League the last game we won was with him inside the pitch. So I told him, 'We need you back soon to win games’.

"I think Antoine is an important player, but we have more players that are playing in his position and doing well, like Iliman [Ndiaye] in this moment, but he needs time to recover."

Man City have won three, drawn two and lost three of their last eight games without Semenyo in all competitions, scoring no goals or just one goal in four of those matches.

The Citizens have once again been heavily reliant on Erling Haaland’s goals this season, but even he has endured a recent blip, failing to make the net ripple in four of his last five matches in all tournaments.

Rayan Cherki has stepped up with two goals in his last three appearances, but Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye – two wide options who compete with Semenyo for starts when everyone is fit – have scored just one goal between them all season.

That is one reason why Semenyo’s imminent return will provide a vital spark for Maresca’s side, who won all seven Premier League matches he featured in before his injury.

Prior to being sidelined in mid-October, Semenyo was averaging a goal involvement every 111 minutes in the top flight with two goals and three assists in seven appearances.

Having already registered 13 goals in 37 appearances  since arriving from Bournemouth in January – including nine goals and four assists in 24 Premier League outings – his directness and proven end product would help ease the scoring burden on Haaland.

#1554. GdS: Super in Serie A, struggling in Europe – the reasons behind the ‘two-faced’ Milan

AC Milan are having a positive start to the 2026-27 season in Serie A, but in the Europa League they have been poor. Why exactly is that the case?

Milan go into tonight’s game against Olympiacos needing a win in order to start putting things right in a competition in which they have so far lost three out of four. The top eight expectation has now vanished, with even a play-off spot in jeopardy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Amorim has been coaching two teams since the summer: one which is excellent in the league with some ups and downs, and another that is frankly terrible when the Europa League anthem players.

Milan score 2.33 goals per game in the league on average, compared to just 1 per game in Europe. All four of those goals in the UEL came in the win over RB Salzburg too: they have drawn a blank in the other three.

Looking a bit deeper, Milan have less possession in Europa League matches (53%, compared to 59% in the league) but shoot 12.5 times per game, more than in Serie A. In Europe they get into the box more often: 26 touches in the opponent’s box compared to 23.

So, why do they score so much less despite being more threatening? Simply put, they shoot worse: the Rossoneri have a very high conversion rate in Serie A (26.4%) which plummets to 10% in Europe. This means that in the UEL it takes 10 shots to score a goal, while in the league it only takes four.

It’s not all mathematics. Anyone who has watched Milan in Europe have noticed their difficulties. At Bournemouth, they were never in the game, against Ferencvaros they collapsed, against Benfica they deserved to lose against a fellow contender.

With just hours to go before the match against the best defence in the competition, another test awaits. However, Amorim must find a way to concede less too. In Europe, Milan concede 1.92 xG per game, while in the league it’s just 1.28.

This all leads to a discussion about line-ups, and Amorim has rotated a lot outside of league action. The right defender has always been Filippo Terracciano or Fikayo Tomori, never Mario Gila. Without the Spaniard, there’s a noticeable difference.

In midfield, Luka Modric has never started, and Adrien Rabiot started only against Salzburg and Ferencvaros. Up front, Diego Moreira started only against Bournemouth. Life, with or without those three, changes completely.

Amorim already knows he won’t have Modric against Olympiacos, but he can plan with Rabiot and Moreira, concocting a strong side despite the injury issues. He’ll ask for overtime tonight and on Monday in Cagliari, knowing his side will then have almost a week to rest.

#1552. Opinion: Liverpool given green light to sign £46m sensation

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players over the last few years.

Over £600 million has been spent on them and, more change is still needed.

Obviously, this isn't the outcome that the Anfield outfit will have wanted but, it's the hand that they've seemingly been dealt.

All of their rivals are constantly looking for ways to upgrade their team and, the more that they manage to do this, the better they become and the more difficult they are to beat.

Fans expected Liverpool to be competing for silverware this term but, now that feels like it all rests on their transfer plans with the club now being handed a green light to sign one of their targets.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool the green light to sign Ronald Araujo

One of the main positions that Liverpool needed to upgrade in the 2026-27 transfer window was their defence.

Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate both exited Anfield for free and, the performances of Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley were shoddy.

Throw in the fact that Bradley managed to suffer yet another long-term injury and, Liverpool were left with a bit-part defence.

That's why Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were brought in.

Nobody knew how each defender would perform due to their lack of Premier League experience but, to the surprise of many, they've been two of the Reds' best players.

But, because Araujo is only on a season-long loan, his future is still undecided or, it was until this fresh update from BBC Sport.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

"At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year."

Ayden Heaven joining Barcelona could force Barcelona to sell Ronald Araujo

Araujo's versatility is one of the best things about him.

The defender can be comfortably used as a centre-back or a right-back with Iraola using him in both positions this term.

Indeed, the Uruguayan's injury history is a bit of a worry but, touch wood, he's managed to keep fit while playing for Liverpool so far.

As mentioned, Araujo's future isn't set in stone yet but, if Barca manage to sign Heaven from Manchester United, it feels like Araujo would fall further down Hansi Flick's plans.

This could mean that the La Liga giants are willing to negotiate a cheaper deal for the centre-back which, judging by the recent developments from Liverpool, is exactly what they want.

Here's hoping that a deal can be reached soon and that Barcelona find a successor for their captain soon.

#1551. A tale of glory or misery in Greece: All the key stats ahead of Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan and Olympiacos will face each other for a fifth time this evening, with the Greek side hosting the Rossoneri in Athens.

The first two meetings came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19. In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent encounters were eight years ago, as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Milan have never won a competitive game against a Greek side in Greece, losing 2 and drawing 4. However, they have lifted the Champions League trophy twice in Athens (4-0 vs. Barcelona in 1994 and 2-1 vs. Liverpool in 2007).

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

#1550. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.
