#1524. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils 'snubbed' by Premier League striker prior to recent contract announcement

By Carter White | 27 Nov 2026 15:20

Manchester United were reportedly snubbed by Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin before he signed a contract extension at Elland Road.

Mauricio Pochettino's men are heading towards a full-blown relegation battle in the top flight this season, with the Red Devils sitting 19th in the Premier League table after winning one of their first 11 matches.

At the other end of the standings, Daniel Farke's Leeds are in seventh position and recently announced a contract extension for talisman Calvert-Lewin, who is now committed to the club until the summer of 2029.

Following his 2025 arrival on a free transfer from Everton, the 29-year-old has established himself as one of the best strikers in the Premier League, as well as earning call-ups to England squads under Thomas Tuchel.

Leeds are supposedly in the market for new attacking options during the winter trading point, however, there is no doubting that Calvert-Lewin will remain a first-choice option in the ranks of the Whites.

According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano via TEAMtalk, Manchester United were keen on bringing Leeds and England star Calvert-Lewin to the Theatre of Dreams during the January transfer window.

However, with the 29-year-old since signing club-record terms at Elland Road, the report claims that the former Everton attacker snubbed the advances of the 20-time English champions.

As well as the out-of-form Red Devils, it is understood that two clubs from Italy were extremely interested in securing the services of Calvert-Lewin during the most recent summer transfer window.

Ultimately, Leeds decided to keep hold of their talent and the player opted to stay put at Elland Road, where Farke's side are looking to push on and secure European qualification this season.

It is believed that Calvert-Lewin has become the highest-paid player in Leeds history by agreeing his new terms, with the Englishman expected to be earning upwards of £110,000 per week.

In the days of Sir Alex Ferguson, plucking one of the Premier League's best strikers from a rival would be relatively simple for Manchester United - see Robin van Persie's 2012 switch from Arsenal as an example.

However, those glory days are long behind the fallen English giants, who are hurtling towards a bottom-three scrap if their form does not seriously improve under new head coach Pochettino.

All things considered, it makes complete sense that Calvert-Lewin snubbed an approach from Man Utd in order to continue building a legacy for Leeds at Elland Road.

Liverpool's big problem with signing a midfielder has been Chelsea. The Blues also need a high-profile midfielder, having sold Enzo Fernandez at the transfer deadline without a replacement.

They did try to sign one, of course. Lamine Camara was a serious option and they did bid. AS Monaco ended the deal right at the death, however, as they felt a bigger one could be had in 2027 - Liverpool were supposedly the reason why, essentially.

Alex Scott is another heavily linked with Liverpool, especially as his former coach, Iraola, is in charge at Anfield. But Chelsea were supposed to be ahead in that race, going all-out for the Bournemouth star.

But David Ornstein reports that Chelsea aren't actually going for a midfielder right now, in what's a massive surprise to everyone. He told USA Sports that he's not aware of any January ideas from the club. Instead, it appears they're going to wait for the summer.

That leaves the door wide open for Liverpool, who could conceivably make a move for an elite midfielder before Chelsea even get to the table. Their biggest rival for competition isn't putting up a fight - and that's a huge advantage in any talks.

It stops the price rising too high, it stops players' heads getting turned, and it also takes away an immediate time pressure to strike a deal. Though, there is still the time pressure of getting it done in January.

But there's no question about it: Chelsea's stance is an advantage for Liverpool if the Reds are still happy to sign a midfield player.

#1522. Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr at centre of African Player of the Year controversy as agent demands transparency

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:21

Ismaila Sarr's agent has launched a fierce criticism of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after the Crystal Palace winger was left off the final five-man shortlist for the 2026 African Player of the Year award, demanding that the governing body publish the full voting results.

The Senegal international enjoyed a remarkable European campaign with Palace, winning the Conference League and finishing as both the competition's leading goalscorer and its Player of the Season. He also scored four goals at the 2026 World Cup, equalling Roger Milla's African record for goals at a single edition of the tournament.

However, Sarr was overlooked in favour of Sadio Mane, Pape Gueye, Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari when the final shortlist was announced on Wednesday, prompting an angry response from his representative, former Premier League forward Diomansy Kamara.

Kamara, who represented Fulham, Portsmouth and West Bromwich Albion during his playing career in England, took to social media on Wednesday evening to question the credibility of the selection process.

The former Senegal international listed Sarr's achievements before demanding that CAF explain how a player with such a record could fail to make the final five.

"We demand transparency, clear criteria and the publication of the detailed voting results," Kamara wrote, before expressing his frustration with the way African football is governed.

Sarr's contribution to Palace's European success was particularly impressive. The 28-year-old scored nine goals in the Conference League, finding the net in both legs of the semi-final against Shakhtar Donetsk. His strike after just 21 seconds in the first leg also established a new record for the fastest goal in the competition's history.

Both his European triumph and his World Cup performances fell within CAF's designated assessment period, which ran from January 1 to September 15, 2026.

One possible explanation for Sarr's absence concerns the timing of the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision to restore Senegal's Africa Cup of Nations title.

Voting for the African Player of the Year award closed on November 20, four days before Senegal were officially reinstated as African champions.

Consequently, voters submitted their selections while Morocco were still officially recognised as the tournament winners, despite Senegal having prevailed on the pitch in January's final.

Another possibility is that support for Senegal's three leading candidates was divided. Mane was named the best player at the Africa Cup of Nations, while Gueye scored the winning goal in the final. Both had strong cases, although neither could match Sarr's individual achievements in European club football and at the World Cup.

CAF has explained that the winners are determined by a voting panel drawn from several areas of African football, including national team coaches and captains, technical experts and journalists. The process is independently monitored by PricewaterhouseCoopers.

There is therefore no evidence that Sarr was deliberately excluded by the governing body. Equally, without a detailed breakdown of the votes, it is impossible to establish whether the timing of the CAS ruling or competition between Senegal's nominees materially affected his candidacy.

The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards ceremony in Lagos on December 2. For Kamara, however, the more pressing issue is establishing how one of the most productive African players in European football failed to make the final shortlist.

#1520. Please, Oliver, can we have some more? Celtic boss Martin O'Neill tells Danish midfielder Sorensen it's time to up his game

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a big reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season

‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I said after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica

‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal

Delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

#1518. Man City owners facing fresh pressure as three Premier League rivals call for forced sale

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 15:42

The owners of Manchester City are facing renewed scrutiny after senior figures at three Premier League clubs reportedly called for them to be forced to sell the club in the wake of its financial breaches.

An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, relating to alleged breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018. The club denies wrongdoing and has appealed against the verdict, with sanctions yet to be determined.

While much of the debate has centred on potential points deductions, financial penalties and the possible removal of titles, some of City's domestic rivals believe that a change of ownership would be necessary to restore confidence in the competition.

Should Man City's owners be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules? ? https://t.co/YfIws1lvS6

According to BBC Sport, senior figures at three Premier League clubs have privately expressed their belief that City's Abu Dhabi owners should be compelled to relinquish control of the club.

One executive, speaking anonymously, suggested that any punishment would be inadequate if the current ownership remained in place, while also questioning the purpose of clubs funding an independent regulator if it was unwilling to intervene in such circumstances.

The independent commission found that City had inflated revenues and concealed losses amounting to approximately £900m through commercial arrangements deemed illegitimate. The findings cover nine seasons, during which City won three Premier League titles.

City strongly dispute those conclusions, arguing that the commission's decision contains fundamental errors of law and fact. Their appeal hearing is expected to take place in December, with a verdict anticipated in the new year.

The latest intervention from rival executives represents a significant development in the wider dispute. Even if City were handed a substantial points deduction or a financial penalty, those measures would not necessarily affect Sheikh Mansour's control of the club.

However, the power to enforce a change of ownership rests with the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), whose responsibilities extend beyond the Premier League's disciplinary framework.

Speaking before a parliamentary committee on Wednesday, IFR chairman David Kogan made it clear that the regulator would not be deterred by the prospect of taking action against one of England's most successful clubs.

"We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

The Football Governance Act 2025 gives the regulator extensive powers over club ownership. Under Section 34, the IFR can assess whether existing owners continue to satisfy suitability requirements, including standards of honesty, integrity and financial soundness.

Should an owner be deemed unsuitable, Section 39 provides a mechanism through which the regulator can require them to relinquish their ownership within a specified period. Section 43 also allows the IFR to issue an ownership removal order and appoint independent trustees to oversee the process where the relevant legal conditions are met.

Such intervention would require a separate assessment of the individuals concerned. An unsuccessful appeal by Manchester City would not, in itself, automatically trigger a sale of the club.

The regulator's independence is particularly significant given Sheikh Mansour's position as vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, alongside the country's extensive economic interests in the United Kingdom.

However, Kogan has insisted that political considerations will have no bearing on the regulator's assessment of the evidence.

For now, the immediate focus remains on City's appeal against the independent commission's findings. Should the verdict be upheld, the club could find themselves facing two separate proceedings: one determining the sporting consequences of the financial breaches and another examining whether the individuals responsible for running the club remain suitable owners and directors.

#1516. Report: Liverpool target now available for €23m, clubs have made enquiries

Liverpool's first-team squad are in need of an upgrade or two.

Without these moves getting made, the Reds will fall even further behind their title rivals and could end up finishing in a worse position than they did last term.

This would be far from ideal as, last term, Arne Slot was sacked for finishing fifth, never mind what would have happened if they'd have finished any lower.

Right now, seven points separate Liverpool and first-placed Arsenal which, in the grand scheme of things, isn't that big of a gap to break down.

But, for them to definitely be able to do this, transfer will need to be made in 2027 to bolster their ranks.

And now, they seem to have been handed a major boost in their pursuit for one player.

Archie Brown has a €23 million release clause in his contract

One main position that Liverpool need to upgrade is their left-back.

Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas have failed to meet expectations this term with fans left wondering what's happened to their defence.

Indeed, Kerkez did have a decent game against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening but, it still feels like more should be coming from him in other games.

Tsimikas is more or less a lost cause and, with his contract set to expire in June 2027, his time at Anfield is over.

These facts have led to questions being asked about the Reds' transfer plans with a fresh update from Florian Plettenberg about Archie Brown certainly something for fans to be excited by.

"Archie Brown has a release clause worth around €23m, valid for both the winter and summer transfer windows. The 23 y/o is a regular starter at Fenerbahçe and has also impressed with some very strong performances in the Champions League," he wrote.

"Under contract until 2028, a move is planned, with Premier League clubs already making enquiries."

Archie Brown would be an interesting signing for Liverpool

Brown has probably only just started to be known by Liverpool fans.

Before the 2026-27 season, it would've been hard to find someone who knew the Englishman within L4.

He's spent most of his career away from England and is currently playing for Fenerbahce.

The left-back had a superb game against Liverpool during the Reds' 3-2 defeat against the Turkish Super Lig outfit in the Champions League which caused several clubs to show an interest in him.

Liverpool were seemingly one of them and, now that it's been revealed that he has a €23 million release clause embedded into his contract, the 24-year-old feels like an absolute steal.

Indeed, it would mean that Liverpool have three left-backs among their ranks for half a season but, it would give the Englishman plenty of time to get settled and start battling Kerkez for the starting role in Iraola's plans.

Brown would also be classed as homegrown which, as everyone knows, is an essential thing for Liverpool at the moment.

#1515. Freddie Potts on the pain of leaving West Ham, why he had to move on this summer, upsetting the odds in the Champions League with Club Brugge - and why they don't fear Liverpool!

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts says. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’

He is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday

Potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’

#1513. Opinion: Julian Ward masterstroke could hand Liverpool a new Virgil van Dijk

Virgil van Dijk has been a constant part of Liverpool's starting XI ever since he joined the club from Southampton back in 2017.

At the time, most people thought that the Reds had massively overpaid for the Dutchman but, after what he's done during his nine years at the club, he's more than repaid their faith.

However, he's now in the final year of his contract and, with him able to speak to foreign clubs about a free transfer by 1 January, a decision needs to be made on his future soon.

Indeed, negotiations were left until the last minute a couple of years ago but, if Andoni Iraola wants to get Liverpool competing for titles again, he needs to be prepared for whatever is thrown his way.

That's why, this latest transfer masterstroke from Julian Ward could be essential to their progress.

Nico Schlotterbeck is going to be Liverpool's next Virgil van Dijk

One of the main things that Van Dijk has is his physical presence.

The 6'4 Dutchman has been the rock at the back for Liverpool for as long as anyone can remember.

Without him, the Reds would have won a lot less trophies than they have.

But, since he'll be 36 years old by the start of the 2026-27 season, Liverpool must figure out if he can continue performing to this level for another two years.

If he can't, a succession plan needs to be put in place with this summer potentially the best time for an amicable parting of ways.

For this to happen, a replacement needs to be sourced because, as good as Giovanni Leoni is likely to be, he's still not played any football for over a year and, since he's never played a minute of Premier League football, nobody knows how good he's actually going to be.

That's why someone such as Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck needs to be targeted.

Nico Schlotterbeck would be a superb transfer for Andoni Iraola

The fact that Van Dijk plays as the left-sided centre-back in Iraola's back four is also a bit of a problem.

Among their ranks at the moment, the Reds have no senior left-footed centre-backs and, most of the defenders they've been linked to are all also right-footed.

Obviously, this hasn't been a problem for Van Dijk but, that doesn't mean it won't be for another defender.

That's why Schlotterbeck, who is left-footed and can also be used as a left-back is perfect.

This, coupled with his Champions League experience, his age (26 years old) and his ability on the ball all make him the perfect successor for the Liverpoool captain.

The German also has a release clause embedded within his contract that can only be activated by certain clubs (Liverpool are rumoured to be one of them) that could play in their favour.

Nobody knows what Iraola's team will look like at the start of the 2027-28 season but, if it includes a team with Schlotterbeck in their defence, they'll be onto a winner.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1510. Amorim explains selection choices, Ferencvaros lessons and responsibility to win consistently

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim knows that results are needed in Europe, but once again stressed that he foresees a ‘long-term project’.

Milan have racked up just three out of 12 points in the first half of the league phase, meaning they really need to change gear if they are to progress into the next round. Tonight’s game is another very tough one on paper, given Olympiacos have 10 points on the board and are in the top eight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim has named a strong starting line-up featuring the likes of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos and the top scorer Alphadjo Cisse. However, what doesn’t help the cause at all are the nine injury absentees, which is noticeable when looking at the bench.

The head coach spoke to Sky in the build-up to kick-off in Greece to shed light on his selections and the importance of learning lessons in Europe. MilanNews relayed his words.

You’ve gone with an attacking side tonight…

“In football, you have to defend and attack. We have to defend with 11 men and attack with 11 men. The players know what positions they have to occupy and are ready.

“We have to be more compact, and even with these attacking players on the pitch, we can defend better than in other Europa League matches.”

Did the players learn their lesson after Ferencvaros?

“I think they understand. We’ve seen videos, we’re working. Against Ferencvaros, we were sluggish because we weren’t compact and focused on the details. In Europe, we need to raise our game and do what we’ve done several times in Serie A.”

Are you ready to prove you can play three good games in a row in a week?

“I think we have to be a great team. To be that, you have to win both in Serie A and in Europe. We have that responsibility. Results matter a lot, obviously, but we’re on a long-term project. We need to understand if we can play during the week, and today will be an additional test.”

#1509. 'That's their problem' – Jose Mourinho sends clear message to Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 16:17

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior are subject to the same selection criteria as the rest of his squad, warning that any dissatisfaction with being named on the bench is a matter for the players themselves.

The Portuguese manager was questioned about the status of his attacking stars during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's La Liga encounter with Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Madrid's recent improvement has coincided with Bellingham's excellent form and a resurgence from Vinicius, who has faced increased competition for his place following the summer arrival of Yan Diomande. Mourinho, however, believes that the collective spirit he has established since returning to the Spanish capital is helping him manage those individual ambitions.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho dismissed the suggestion that certain members of his squad enjoy preferential treatment.

"If one day they are on the bench and they don't like it, that's their problem," said the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager, who stressed that Mbappe, Bellingham and Vinicius were on an equal footing with their teammates.

Mourinho acknowledged that Mbappe has yet to start a match on the bench this season, while Bellingham has only done so once. He explained that the difference in playing time between the pair and other members of the squad was justified by their performances.

Mbappe has registered 19 goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, while Bellingham demonstrated his importance to the team once again in Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Madrid were trailing at half time when Mourinho introduced the England international, who subsequently scored a superb goal and provided the assist for Vinicius to complete the scoring.

Such performances help explain why Mourinho has been reluctant to rest either player. The Portuguese nevertheless insisted that the team's objectives take precedence over individual ambitions and expressed satisfaction at how his players have accepted that principle.

The debate surrounding Madrid's attacking options has intensified in recent weeks, with Vinicius returning to form after a difficult start to the campaign and a four-match La Liga suspension.

The Brazilian made an important contribution from the bench in last weekend's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo before finding the net against PSV, giving Mourinho another selection decision to make ahead of the Alaves fixture.

However, Mourinho rejected the idea that Vinicius and Diomande should be regarded as rivals, explaining that both players share the same objectives and that the Brazilian has retained the support of his teammates throughout his difficult spell.

The Madrid boss also dismissed concerns about the atmosphere within the dressing room, revealing that he has not encountered any significant problems during his first five months back at the club.

His satisfaction with the current squad extends to his plans for the January transfer window, with Mourinho making it clear that he would prefer to finish the season with the players already at his disposal.

"I don't want anyone to leave either; the door is closed," the Portuguese explained after ruling out the need for new signings.

That stance is particularly noteworthy given the limited opportunities afforded to some of Madrid's younger attacking players. With Rodrygo also working his way back from a long-term injury, competition for places could become even greater during the second half of the campaign.

Mourinho's comments suggest that he would rather manage that competition internally than reduce his attacking options midway through a season in which Madrid are competing for honours on several fronts.

#1508. They didn't think he was this good: Star proves Liverpool completely wrong

Liverpool did not think one star was this good. He's proven them completely wrong and made some people look foolish.

Liverpool made some bold decisions in the summer as they looked to reshape the side after a difficult campaign. Of course, that came one year after reshaping the side on the back of a successful campaign.

Regardless, things did need to happen and part of that was Liverpool locking down two midfielders: Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. The pair were given massive new contracts as the club committed to them as the core of their midfield.

It was a bold decision and a brave one. Liverpool picked two players without a history of playing alongside one another while also committing to a head coach who plays with a two-man midfield.

But the bravery was also seen in who they didn't commit to - an inevitable consequence of deciding on two players to lead the way forward. And you've got to say that they got that one wrong.

Alexis Mac Allister is the one Liverpool said no to. Literally, in fact, as he asked for a new contract and was told the club wasn't in position to give him one. And that was right after they'd offered and agreed deals with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai.

It was a real message to people that Liverpool wanted to move on from Mac Allister and build around the other two. That's how Mac Allister took it, anyway, as he publicly discussed how disappointed he was with the club's stance.

Fast-forward a few months, though, and things look different. There is absolutely no question that Mac Allister has been the standout midfielder for Liverpool this season and any belief on the club's part that he was past his prime has been proven completely incorrect.

Andoni Iraola has come to rely on him above nearly any other player. Mac Allister is the core of midfield and in some ways, the core of the side - the one who does a bit of everything to make sure it all knits together.

So not only is Mac Allister the best midfielder right now, he's also the easiest one to build around. It's making the contract decisions earlier this year look foolish, honestly.

But perhaps Liverpool recognise that. The Mail is just one outlet reporting that they're to open talks with Mac Allister's father in the coming weeks as they look to find a compromise over a new contract.

#1507. Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

#1505. Como vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 16:43, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 16:48

Midweek winners in Europe, Como and Juventus will resume their pursuit of Serie A's top four when they clash at Stadio Sinigaglia on Sunday.

Both teams are on track to qualify directly for the last 16 in their continental campaigns, but they currently trail Italy's top quartet.

Ascending to third place in the Champions League table - above the likes of Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona - Como continued their incredible European exploits on Tuesday evening, with a 1-0 home win over AEK Athens.

The little Lombardy club are firmly on course to reach the knockout phase on their continental debut, and they are still in an open Serie A title race.   Though they recently lost to Inter Milan once again, normal service was resumed last weekend, when Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Sinigaglia.

Victory kept them in touch with both Milan sides and the two unbeaten Rome clubs, and the Lariani have claimed a club record 26 points from their first 12 top-flight fixtures.

Unbeaten as hosts this season, Cesc Fabregas has seen his team concede just one goal in five home games, including four consecutive clean sheets - against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia and Cagliari.

Como now face a crucial clash in the fight for Champions League qualification, and success on Sunday would open up an eight-point lead over Juventus.

Before doing the double over Juve last season, they had not beaten the Turin giants at home since 1952, but a pair of 2-0 wins helped them sneak past the Bianconeri to claim fourth place in the end.

Reflecting their sudden change in status, Juventus have never before faced Como while trailing in the Serie A standings, yet that is now the situation they face.

While the Lariani were dining at Europe’s top table, Juve extended their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League in midweek, defeating Omonia 4-1 in Turin.

Posing a potential solution to their striker problems, Jeff Ekhator found the net on his first start for the club, and across all competitions the Bianconeri have scored 14 goals across their last five games.

In Europe, Juventus are set to cruise through as one of the top eight finishers - having claimed 13 points from a possible 15 so far - but it has been a more mixed picture on the domestic scene.

Despite thumping Venezia 4-0 last week, Luciano Spalletti's injury-hit squad lag 11 points behind league leaders Lazio in sixth place, partly due to their sub-par away form.

Juve’s Serie A record on the road is two wins, two draws and two defeats - with eight goals scored and eight conceded - so visiting Como will surely cause some concern.

Como are still missing ex-Juventus striker Moise Kean, plus Willy Kambwala and Jesus Rodriguez, but Fabregas could have two wingers back from injury this weekend.

Jayden Addai and Assane Diao both face fitness tests, while midfielder Maxence Caqueret is a strong doubt.

Without Kean, Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the Lariani’s front line, having scored 11 goals in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Juve’s top Serie A scorer is Brazilian centre-back Bremer with a modest three goals, though Nick Woltemade has been directly involved in three across his last two league games and is faring well in the Europa League.

The German striker must compete with Ekhator and Randal Kolo Muani to start at the Sinigaglia, where Spalletti will be without several key men.

Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined, while Nico Gonzalez remains a doubt; more positively, Kerim Alajbegovic and Pierre Kalulu could both be named on the bench.

Butez; Couto, Chalobah, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Luiz, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, McKennie, Kolo Muani; Woltemade

Two of Italy's tightest defences will face off on Sunday night: since Spalletti's arrival in Turin last November, Juventus have kept 19 clean sheets and Como have 20.

While the hosts have been far more convincing, Juve are putting together a good run of results and their long absence list is starting to clear.

#1500. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

#1497. It's official Liverpool promote sensational left-back, he's the next Andy Robertson

An exciting left-back has been promoted to Liverpool's first-team.

Milos Kerkez is getting back to his best. With his former manager Andoni Iraola's guidance the young Hungarian, yes it's easy to forget, he is still young, is playing like the version that we all fell in love with at Bournemouth.

Over the last year, Liverpool's players have faced a lot of criticism. Some of it, probably rightly. But others have been over the top, such is the nature of social media these days.

Fans clamour to individual performances when they are good and praise the players who produced them as deities. But they quickly, incredibly quickly, turn into villains if they produce a bad performance.

With Kerkez, he is still learning his trade. He is a young player who was thrust into a new role under Arne Slot - who lacked a bit of confidence when Iraola arrived as a result but is now finding his feet again.

Liverpool still need a left-backThat is not to say because Kerkez is producing that the need for a new left-back to come in isn't there. Kostas Tsimikas cannot be relied on as a deputy. Liverpool need to recruit someone else to provide competition and adept cover for Kerkez. It's imperative that is resolved in the coming windows and will be one of the main objectives for Julian Ward as he takes control of the sporting director position. Who could be targeted? Well Neco Williams could be an easy solution but the costs might be significant. Liverpool also have the likes of Lewis Hall on their radar, and other players like Mahamadou Nagida will be well-liked by the club as well. But there is also an internal solution.

That is not to say because Kerkez is producing that the need for a new left-back to come in isn't there. Kostas Tsimikas cannot be relied on as a deputy.

Liverpool need to recruit someone else to provide competition and adept cover for Kerkez.

It's imperative that is resolved in the coming windows and will be one of the main objectives for Julian Ward as he takes control of the sporting director position.

Well Neco Williams could be an easy solution but the costs might be significant. Liverpool also have the likes of Lewis Hall on their radar, and other players like Mahamadou Nagida will be well-liked by the club as well.

That solution is Scottish youth international Cameron Williams, who has been catching the eye in the academy recently.

Williams trained with Scotland's senior national team when he was just 16-years-old. He is a highly talented left-back, with excellent qualities going forward, who many regard as the new Andy Robertson.

The youngster has struggled with a few injuries here and there. However, he is now back playing regularly for the club's U18 side and has subsequently earned himself an official promotion.

Looking at Liverpool's squad on the UEFA website, Williams has been added to the team through the B-list, as highlighted by Lewis Bower as well.

It means Williams is now officially a member of the first-team squad and could even feature in the Champions League. A player to keep a close eye on!

#1496. Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan: Hutchinson inspires remarkable comeback in Greece

AC Milan produced a stunning come-from-behind victory against Olympiacos, scoring four times unanswered to win 4-2.

It looked like being another miserable European night for Milan, as they fell two goals behind inside 50 minutes. The first was given as a Mike Maignan own-goal after Lorenzo Pirola’s header from a corner hit the crossbar then the goalkeeper, then Jota Silva doubled the advantage.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Out of nowhere, Milan mounted a comeback inside 15 second-half minutes. Omari Hutchinson inspired it, scoring a wonderful solo goal to halve the deficit, then setting up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser, and also providing the assist for Christian Pulisic’s goal off the bench.

Diego Moreira finished a counter-attack right at the end of the game to make it 4-2 and seal the result, one that was very much needed for Milan given their start in the competition. The play-off hopes have been dealt a big boost, while the top eight could still be a possibility too.

Amorim made four changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Frosinone on Sunday. Two were enforced due to injuries, with Ardon Jashari replacing Luka Modric and Pervis Estupinan taking Davide Bartesaghi’s spot. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchinson came into the attack.

The first shot of the game took less than two minutes to come and it provided an example of the intense pressing that the home side have become known for, though Freuler’s effort from distance was a speculative one that sailed comfortably over.

Milan began to string some nice moves together, and they had a couple of attempts of their own from just beyond the edge of the box miss the target. The first came from Cisse, who cut inside and curled one well over and wide, then Jashari concluded a promising attack with a wild shot.

There were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

The first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

Olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

The trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Milan were inches away from getting themselves level quickly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. A ball over the top found Cisse’s run in behind and Ortega came darting off his line but the ball squirmed through. The Italian somehow got a shot off from the floor that was rolling into the net but for Lirola’s last-ditch sliding clearance for a corner.

There was a flash point towards the end of the half which saw De Winter and Jota Silva both go into the box. A long ball over the top was eventually followed by play being blown dead for offside, yet the pair had a stand-up wrestling match for about 20 yards, until they both even ended up off the field.

In the first of two minutes added on at the end of the half, Pirola had a chance to actually get his name on the scoresheet after the opener was labelled an own-goal. Some dire defending down the right ended with a cut-back that the former Inter youth academy man fired over from inside the box.

Amorim chose to make two changes at the break, as the American duo Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah came on. Ramos and Estupinan were the ones to make way, with Cisse going up front and Moreira switching over to left wing-back.

Within four minutes of the restart, Olympiacos doubled their lead after yet more calamitous defending. De Winter continued his trend of failing to strong together multiple games without errors as he played a stray pass out from the back, allowing Freuler to play though Jota Silva, who fired past Maignan first time.

De Winter then gave away a sloppy foul when it looked like he had brought a ball under his control and Amorim had seen enough, bringing Fikayo Tomori on for the Belgian.

Just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. Having seized possession inside his own half, the Englishman went on a brilliant solo run down the right where he was nearly clipped down twice, before jinking inside onto his preferred left foot and finding the bottom corner with a precise low shot.

Milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. A sustained period of possession inside the Olympiacos half saw the ball worked nicely down the right side for Hutchinson to cross perfectly onto the head of Cisse at the far post, who headed in from a few yards out for his 10th of the campaign.

As if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. The substitute struck his volley perfectly, nestling it inside the post.

Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

With just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays showed it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

#1495. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery, Damian Vidagany deliver contradictory Alejandro Garnacho messages

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 17:31

Unai Emery and Damian Vidagany have seemingly contradicted each other with regards to Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future

Having been omitted from three Villa squads in a row, the Chelsea loanee has been a hot topic for debate.

After Emery quickly decided against activating a £35m option to sign Liverpool's Harvey Elliott in 2025-26, Garnacho being frozen out after seven substitute appearances when a £43m permanent transfer could become an obligation if a certain amount of matches are played appears to be close to an identical situation.

At a press conference on Friday, Emery insisted that he 'respected' Garnacho but was choosing to select other players.

Emery also claimed that "the club is running" matters during the winter transfer window. However, Vidagany told a club forum on Thursday that Emery was in full control.

Vidagany - the club's head of football operations - says that Villa chiefs "follow Unai Emery" and that the Spaniard has "full power" over transfers.

He said: "I know that is a topic that everyone wants to know. You can give me 3,000 lbs of pressure, but there is only one fact. In Aston Villa, the sporting decisions are taken by Unai Emery.

"Emery decides if a player will or will not be in the squad according to the criteria of Unai Emery. Emery is picking other players and decided not to put him in the squad.

"This can change or not, I don't know. It will depend maybe on the performance of the player. We are a club who tries to be efficient with the resources we have.

"There is no question that Emery has full power on who is in the squad and who is not. Any noise outside of us, it is something that we don't want to control or discuss.

"We follow Unai Emery, he is our leader. He knows deeper than anyone what the squad needs."

When Aston Villa loaned Garnacho from Chelsea, it was widely claimed that it would be easier to activate the set amount of appearances required for a permanent transfer to proceed than with Elliott.

Elliott needed to make 10 appearances. With Garnacho having made seven substitute outings before being frozen out, the assumption is that eight or nine matches is the so-called magic number.

Villa have no loan break option that they can enforce, nor do Chelsea have a recall clause. Therefore, if the clubs cannot reach a fresh agreement over financial terms, Garnacho faces the realistic prospect of not playing again in 2026-27.

Garnacho is, theoretically, available for selection for seven more matches to be played this year.

#1493. Opinion: Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold passes audition, what a player

Liverpool's next Trent Alexander-Arnold may now be known. He's passed his audition in front of Andoni Iraola and co. - now he can be signed.

Liverpool lost Trent Alexander-Arnold to Real Madrid in 2025 and with that, one of their best creative players disappeared. A unique one, too - no one in the history of football has done what Alexander-Arnold can do from right-back.

We don't think that's too controversial. The Scouser's ability to create and progress the ball from a full-back position is unheard of and he was a core reason why Liverpool were such a standout side during his time at the club.

But with Alexander-Arnold's exit, the Reds knew they had to move in a different director. Conor Bradley was chosen to be first-choice, though injuries have essentially ruined that plan. It might get back on track, but it's a waiting game involving a lot of hope.

Jeremie Frimpong is an entirely different full-back to Alexander-Arnold. To the extent that he's arguably not even a full-back but a wing-back. The Dutchman hasn't ever made the role his own, unable to offer solidity while his attacking game feels too limited to be a threat with another wide player on that side.

So how about going back to the Alexander-Arnold way? It's difficult for as we've said, he's essentially unique in football for what he can do. But there is a player who looks like he could replicate it.

Kyriani Sabbe: Maybe Liverpool's answerMake no mistake: Club Brugge are a fantastic side and Liverpool's 3-0 win in Belgium was a brilliant one. Make no mistake: Club Brugge are a fantastic side and Liverpool's 3-0 win in Belgium was a brilliant one. They kept a clean sheet against a team that usually dominates, even if they had to ride their luck at times.

One notable facet of that match is that Liverpool didn't have the majority of possession against a Belgian side. This Brugge iteration is a brilliant one with some brilliant players.

One of those is Kyriani Sabbe, who is doing notable things from right-back. He's someone averaging over 100 touches per 90 minutes - a ridiculous figure for a right-back but he's a player Brugge turn to for progression.

It was the same against Liverpool on Wednesday. Sabbe had the fourth-most touches in the match and second-most for Brugge as they won the possession battle.

Notably, Sabbe used these touches to move his side forward. His 12 line-breaking passes were five more than any of the four players with more touches than him, and only Jeremy Jacquet managed more in the match (13).

And that number is fewer than Sabbe usually manages. He's averaging an absolutely ridiculous 17 per 90 minutes in Belgium this season, to go along with a long-ball success rate of 56 per cent.

So here's a 21-year-old with the kind of passing numbers you'd only really see from Alexander-Arnold. And he's doing it in the UEFA Champions League and in a successful side that's used to lots of possession.

It makes Sabbe an incredibly interesting prospect and one that Liverpool simply must look at as they look to solve their right-back problem. Wednesday felt like an audition of sorts and one that the player certainly passed.

#1490. Porto vs Sporting Lisbon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 27 Nov 2026 17:42, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 19:03

Porto will look to maintain their perfect start to the league season when they welcome Sporting Lisbon to Estadio do Dragao for Sunday's matchday 12 headline fixture.

The Dragons have won all 11 of their league matches to sit top of the Primeira Liga table, five points clear of second-placed Benfica and nine ahead of the third-placed Lions.

Francesco Farioli has made an impressive start to his second season in charge of Porto after leading the team to the title last term, and the Dragons are now just two victories away from matching their best start to a top-flight campaign, having won their first 13 matches in 1939-40.

The Blue and Whites, who recorded a league-high 21 clean sheets and conceded just 18 goals in the Primeira Liga last campaign, have maintained their defensive solidity this term, allowing a league-low five goals and registering the joint-most shutouts (six).

Porto's most recent outing in the Portuguese top flight was a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Vitoria de Guimaraes, in an encounter where Martim Fernandes scored an 86th-minute winner to preserve the Dragons' flawless record in the top flight.

Farioli's men have also put their continental campaign back on track, with a 1-0 victory away to Feyenoord in midweek marking their second consecutive Champions League win and lifting the Blue and Whites to 22nd in the 36-team table after they lost their opening three fixtures in the competition.

Porto have now won six of their last seven matches across all competitions in regulation time, with the only exception being a penalty shootout victory over lower-division Paredes to reach the last 16 of the Taca de Portugal, where they will face Leiria on December 17.

Looking to extend their perfect league run, Farioli’s charges can also draw confidence from their impressive home form, having won all five of their Primeira Liga matches at the Dragao this season while scoring at least twice in each, including a 3-1 success over Benfica in September's O Classico.

However, Sporting have the opportunity to become the latest major obstacle in that pursuit, with the visitors arriving with renewed confidence following their recent managerial change, which saw Paulo Fonseca replace Rui Borges in early November.

The 53-year-old, who previously managed Porto during the 2013-14 campaign, oversaw a 1-0 league win over Moreirense in his first game in charge of his current club, with Luis Suarez scoring the winner, before guiding the Lions to another victory in the Taca de Portugal against Uniao de Serra.

Sporting's most recent outing was a chaotic 2-2 draw with Manchester United on Wednesday, leaving the Lisbon outfit ninth in the Champions League table while extending their unbeaten run to five matches (W4, D1) across all competitions.

The Lions have also avoided defeat in all five of their league away games this season (W3, D2), but Sunday's clash presents a different challenge, given they have managed just two victories in their last 19 Primeira Liga meetings (D9, L8) with Porto and are winless in their last 10 top-flight visits to the Dragao (D5, L5), drawing each of the most recent three.

Porto will be without Gabriel Mec, Vasco Sousa (broken leg) and former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling (knee) as they continue their respective recoveries from injury.

Santiago Gimenez led the line in the victory over Feyenoord, but Samu Aghehowa could reclaim the number nine spot following his starts in the Dragons' last two league matches, although Andre Silva remains in contention, having recorded more minutes than the other two forwards in the Primeira Liga this season.

As for Sporting, Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos returned to training earlier in the week following spells on the sidelines, although this encounter could come too soon for both players

Luis Suarez is expected to lead the line once again, with the Colombian, who won the Golden Boot with 28 league goals last season, having already found the net nine times in the Primeira Liga this term, leaving him two behind Benfica's Vangelis Pavlidis.

Heavyweight derbies such as this are difficult to call, regardless of form or momentum, and Sporting's recent performances suggest they have enough quality to make life uncomfortable for the league leaders.

Furthermore, three of the last five meetings between the sides across all competitions have ended in draws so we are backing another stalemate, which would bring the Dragons' flawless league run to an end.
