#1489. Report: Liverpool face transfer threat as club opens up contract talks

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of transfers this season.

Nobody knows exactly what's going to happen in the January window or even the 2027-28 summer window but, change is almost certainly afoot.

Without that, Liverpool will fall even further behind their title rivals and cause themselves more harm than good.

January is a notoriously hard time for clubs to agree deals with teams from across the globe demanding more money than usual due to the restricted time available to replace their players.

However, that doesn't mean it's impossible to get some over the line with one club now trying their luck with a Liverpool star.

Trabzonspor have opened up contract talks with Virgil van Dijk

One of the main players to have been linked with a Liverpool exit this summer is Virgil van Dijk.

The Dutchman's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, since Liverpool don't know whether he's going to be able to keep his performance levels this high for another two years, they're waiting to decide whether he's worth another deal or not.

Most fans believe that he is because, on the market right now, there are little to no options available for Liverpool to explore, not ones that wouldn't cost a fortune, anyway.

But, because another two years will obviously be a lot of money for the Reds to commit to, they need to be 100% sure about their decision.

So, thanks to their stalling, media outlets have started to link Van Dijk with a move away from Liverpool with A Spor now sharing an update on the 35 year old's future.

"Trabzonspor, which caused a stir with the signings of Mohamed Salah , Andre Onana , and Fabinho, is showing no signs of slowing down in the transfer market," they wrote.

"It has been claimed that the Black Sea representative has begun official negotiations for 35-year-old veteran defender Virgil van Dijk, who is in the final year of his contract with Premier League giant Liverpool .

"While it is not yet clear whether the transfer will be finalized during the mid-season break or at the end of the season."

Liverpool can only let Virgil van Dijk go if they sign a replacement or have one lined up

Van Dijk has been Liverpool's rock at the back for as long as anyone can remember now.

The Dutchman has been their leader and is one of the main reasons why they've been so successful.

Without signing him in 2017, it feels like the Reds would have been nowhere near as dominant as they were.

Right now, they're trying to get back to that era and, while that's going to be difficult, it's certainly something that they can do.

But, if they sell Van Dijk and don't sign a replacement or at least have one lined up for the summer, they're going to dig themselves into a massive hole.

Nico Schlotterbeck, Jacobo Ramon and even Murillo are all solid options for Liverpool to explore but, if they don't get a deal for at least one new centre-back done before they allow Van Dijk to leave, some serious questions will need to be asked.

Here's hoping that Julian Ward and Iraola have a plan in mind.

#1487. NEC vs FC Twente - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 27 Nov 2026 17:49, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 17:52

Back in Eredivisie action after their respective European commitments, NEC and FC Twente meet at Stadion de Goffert on Sunday.

Dick Schreuder's men are 12th in the Eredivisie table and remain within touching distance of teams currently in the drop zone, which highlights how underwhelming their league campaign has been compared to last season’s unprecedented success.

With no wins in any of the last five encounters, recent matches against Twente do not hold happy memories for NEC, who are seeking a first victory since January 2024 to avoid suffering consecutive league defeats for the first time this season.

Yet to keep a clean sheet in 2026-27, Sunday’s hosts have plenty of room for improvement defensively. A shutout this weekend would be a good starting point, particularly against opponents who have scored 11 times across the last five meetings.

Twente are averaging three goals per game across their six away league outings - thanks in no small part to November 1’s 9-0 demolition of SBV Excelsior - this season, so NEC’s issues at the back will definitely be music to their ears. However, the Enschede-based outfit did come up short in their last assignment on the road.

Days after coming back for a third game running en route to a 2-1 win over Willem II, Twente looked set to secure another positive result from behind in Thursday’s Conference League clash against Freiburg, where they trailed initially but managed to level proceedings through Younes Taha, only for Jan-Niklas Beste to net a stoppage-time winner.

That ended a six-match winless run for the Tukkers, and they will now seek to get back to winning ways, having not lost back-to-back competitive matches since July.

Like NEC (12/21), John van den Brom’s men have scored most of their goals (19/32) after half time, hinting that this weekend’s clash could come to life as it progresses, so supporters should not be in a hurry to leave if it proves a slow burner.

With their title rivals scheduled to be in action earlier, Sunday’s visitors risk losing crucial ground if they fail to claim maximum points in the final fixture of matchday 14.

Bram Nuytinck and Philippe Sandler are confirmed defensive absentees for NEC, while Emre Mor is also unavailable for Sunday’s match.

Perr Schuurs has missed the last three games and remains a major doubt, so Ahmetcan Kaplan is likely to marshal the defence once again.

Bryan Linssen has netted four times across his last three home matches for the hosts, and the 36-year-old will be aiming to deliver once again.

Max Bruns, Krzysztof Kurowski, Filip Erik Thorvaldsen, Lars Unnerstall, and Thomas van den Belt will miss the trip to Nijmegen as Twente continue to contend with injury problems.

Sondre Orjasaeter has registered a goal contribution in both of his two appearances for Twente against NEC and will be keen to extend that run.

Crettaz; Bras, Kaplan, Fonville; Kers, Nejasmic, Lebreton, Bakker; Chery, Tadic, Linssen

Drommel; Adelgaard, Nijstad, Propper, Van Rooy; Weidmann, Zerrouki; Orjasaeter, Taha, Rots; Weghorst

Both teams have scored in four of the last five meetings between Twente and NEC, suggesting a clean sheet for either side may be unlikely on Sunday.

However, Twente possess greater quality across the pitch and should have enough to claim all three points.

#1486. Player Ratings: Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan – Hutchinson unplayable; Pulisic class

AC Milan completed a crucial comeback as they scored four goals against Olympiacos in the second half. One man in particular was behind the Rossoneri’s resurgence and below are the player ratings.

49 minutes into the game, it looked like Ruben Amorim and his men were heading for another disappointing defeat in the Europa League. Then, Omari Hutchinson decided enough was enough and inspired his teammates to a massive comeback.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Hutchinson (9.5 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

👎 De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

👔 Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

Maignan (6): He made a great save in the first half to deny Martins. Some have suggested that he could have come out to parry the corner away on the first goal, but I don’t entirely agree. Anyway, he couldn’t do much about the second goal and was okay with his feet.

Gila (7): He was his usual aggressive self and that helped Milan on several occasions. Perhaps more so than his ability to win the ball back, however, it was his clearances that meant the most as he stopped some very good crosses. He also had a great overlapping run before the Rossoneri’s second goal.

De Winter (4.5): He has to take full responsibility for the second goal. It was truly a horrible pass and he then kept the goalscorer onside due to poor positioning. I actually don’t think he was good with his passing in the first half either, so the rating feels deserved.

Diawara (5): Touch and judgment. Those are the two things that let him down tonight. He put himself in too many tough positions due to the touch, and his judgment didn’t help when it came to anticipating the passes over the top. Just a really poor display, sadly.

Estupinan (5.5): He wasn’t terrible, but not good either. A rather quiet performance from him when you think about it, so it wasn’t enough for a pass here.

Jashari (6): It was a good opportunity for him and he sort of took it, I guess? It was very much a decent display overall. He had that great pass for Cisse that nearly led to a goal and also helped well in the build-up. However, he had a few misplaced passes and perhaps could have done more to stop Pirola in his tracks before the first goal.

Rabiot (6): In fairness to him, he did have a couple of important clearances defensively but in attack, he definitely didn’t add as much as we have seen in recent weeks. The goal contributions streak had to come to an end at some point. Still, overall, it was an okay performance.

Moreira (7): The goal obviously helps his rating a lot, especially since he remained composed, but he also had a couple of really nice switches to Hutchinson on the other side. He was a tad wasteful in some situations, in my opinion, but a decent display plus a goal deserves a good rating.

Hutchinson (9.5 – MOTM): Absolutely unstoppable in that second half. I mean, WOW! It’s not like a tap-in brought him to life either. He took matters into his own hands and scored an amazing solo goal, starting in Milan’s own half. Then the two assists on top of that, and the hockey assist for the fourth. Again, wow!

Cisse (7.5): Another goal for the youngster! I thought he did well at left-wing, nearly scoring that goal despite the goalkeeper’s challenge, but he continued to do well at centre-forward. The movement and header on the goal proved once again that he’s got it.

Ramos (5.5): Similarly to Estupinan, as both were taken off at half-time, it was more a quiet performance than it was a really bad one. That said, the No.9 had a couple of moments on the counter that could have been handled better.

Musah (6.5): It’s hard to put my finger on exactly what he changed, but he brought something to the game which helped Milan play better. Could absolutely be his movement as he covered a lot of ground and wasn’t afraid to drive forward either.

Pulisic (8.5): World class is probably the best way to describe him. You could immediately see the difference he was going to make, although perhaps no one predicted that goal. It was a tremendous strike to complete the turnaround for Milan. Tremendous! And then he got the assist for Moreira. We can forgive the miss just before that.

Tomori (6.5): Almost a 7 for him, but it’s possible that I might be influenced by just how poor De Winter and Diawara were. Anyway, the Englishman returned with a strong performance and showed that he’s one to rely on.

Terracciano (6): He’s the master of always opting for the easy way out, but in this case, that was probably exactly what Milan needed.

Amorim (7): I think he deserves a bit of credit as Milan’s first half was far from bad. They looked a lot more switched on compared to previous Europa League outings, and the goals could have been avoided through more player effort. Then, he made all the right substitutions.

🚨Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil on AC Milan’s 15-minute comeback against Olympiacos:

We lost today because we failed to do our assignment on Omari Hutchinson.

We initially had a plan to contain him and keep him quiet. We wanted to stop him receiving the ball facing our defenders, because once he turns and starts running at you, the problem becomes much bigger.

And for most of the first half, we did it.

Even in the second half, for some time, we managed it.

Hutchinson started taking responsibility.

And suddenly our defensive structure was changing because everybody was worried about him.

We actually removed two players from marking him because we wanted to protect the space around him.

He got the better of Onyemachi, scored the first goal and suddenly Milan believed again.

I was angry with my players because we allowed him to get into those situations.

When you are 2–0 up at home against AC Milan, you cannot allow one player to turn the entire match around.

There is very little you can do when you have a winger running at you with that much confidence.

He is small, he is close to the ground, his balance is excellent and he changes direction very quickly.

That makes him extremely difficult to defend.

If you go to ground, you risk catching his leg instead of the ball and getting a yellow card.

If you don’t go to ground, he pushes the ball past you and runs.

So the defender has to make a decision in one second.

Our defenders decided to give him the space.

And once he realised they were backing away from him, he became even more confident.

That is when you know you have a problem.

Because a winger like that doesn’t need five chances.

Give him one successful dribble and suddenly he believes he can beat everybody.

We went from controlling the game to defending like we were frightened of one player.

We should have made somebody stay close to him instead of allowing him to receive the ball and face our defence.

But football punishes you when you hesitate.

We went from a perfect win to a perfect defeat in fifteen minutes.

Because I don’t think we were the worse team.

I don’t think our football suddenly disappeared.

We simply failed to deal with one player when the game became chaotic.

I told him, ‘You have a very good player there.’

Because if Hutchinson learns how to control games like that consistently, not just moments, then Milan have something very special.

And unfortunately for us, we allowed him to do it.”

Amazing to see Pulisic make such a difference. His movement opened up the match. The goal too was fabulous.

Of course, Omari was the primary difference maker in this match. What a solo goal. It will go down in our memories. And two gorgeous assists. Still, without Puli coming on we don’t win.

Omari’s performance in the 2nd half was a 10.0, but in the 1st half he was only slightly above average, so that brings it down.

For me, I’ll go with Omari at a 9.0 and Puli 8.5.

Other highest marks for me go to Cisse and Moreira, but neither was above a 7.5.

Cisse – Great header and great nose for goal, ties up the match, but he really needs to improve his vision and passing and dial down the selfishness a bit. His goal was great, but his next two touches should have been passes, but he tried ridiculous shots. 7.0

Moreira – Tons of energy and grinta and just a player I like a lot, but he was also sloppy at times in this game. Awful set piece attempt. Should have passed more quickly in several instances. Nice goal on the last kick of the game. 7.5

Maingan – I too think he should have come out for the corner kick. And then it’s an own goal off his back. The saves weren’t terribly difficult nor was his play with his feet good enough to redeem him. Key player for us, but this was not his best. 5.5

Jashari – I like this player and was really ready to love this performance, but at the end of the day it was average at best. A bit anonymous. He made several great passes but also made far too many sideways and backwards moves. Maybe we’re spoiled by Modric’s amazing inimitable style, but Jashari just doesn’t seem ambitious enough. He might still develop, I’m not sure, let’s try him a few more times, but this was not the big show we wanted to see. 6.0

Gila — solid on the ball and some great clearances, too aggressive at times. He does raise the level of our defense overall, and made some good one v one stops. 6.5

Koni — Poor, but I’m not quite as low on his game as others. Yes, the second goal was on him, but it wasn’t an awful giveaway, just a long ball that wasn’t hit hard or high enough, and the opponent made a great header to intercept it and place it into a teammate’s path. Koni did make some great interceptions. 5.5

Diawara – Not good enough on the ball and got beat several times. I like how this player is developing, but he was not great today. 5.5.

Estupinan – Poor passing, little energy going forward, but didn’t get beat too badly. I’m ready to move on from this guy. 5.0

Rabiot – Not one of his vintage matches, but not awful. He is such a classy player that even subpar performances from him are decent. 6.0

Ramos – I just don’t see the longterm path here for this guy. We paid a lot for him, and he does some good things, but he’s actually not great on the ball. He can’t hold it up, and he is sometimes sloppy with even unpressured possession. I’d like to see Cisse start every other match for the next month, and see how that goes. 5.0

In addition to Puli, I think Musah and Tomori were both huge positive difference makers. Amorim making good subs and good adjustments.

Musah adds a lot in termis of physicality and energy in the midfield, and he won the ball that lead to Puli’s winner. 7.0

Tomori brought great energy and concentration and I’d like to see more of him. 7.0.

Terracciano – This guy is simply not at the level and should be sold asap. I’ve been saying it since day one. He scares me and always looks about to give the ball away. He doesn’t have the skill on the ball to simply make a dummy or pause a pass, as we saw when he was in the corner and panicked and played the ball off of Moreira instead of the simple pass to Jashari. Luckily in this game, this didn’t hurt us, and he actually didn’t get beat. 5.0

Commotto – barely touched the ball, seemed shy and overawed. In one moment he could have taken the ball upfield but was too tentative. Could be a great player that just needs more time, but for this match he made no positive contributions and slightly hurt us. 5.0

While it started out a bit like our matches against other top level Europa opponents (Benfica, Bournemouth), this was much better even in the first half. We were never outmatched. And Amorim outcoached our opponents by making great adjustments at halftime and gambled a bit by taking Ramos and Estu off at halftime. 7.5

Taking off Ramos alone gives +2 rating points

Going forward the key to AC is the teams ability to get healthy, tight lines Billy

#1485. Man City news: Erling Haaland is “upset” as Enzo Maresca responds to concerns before Arsenal showdown

By Oliver Thomas | 27 Nov 2026 17:56

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has insisted that he has "no problem at all" with Erling Haaland, despite admitting that the Norwegian striker is "upset" amid the club's recent slump in form.

The Citizens made a positive start to life under new boss Maresca, winning 11 of their first 12 matches in all competitions in which Haaland scored 13 goals.

However, City have since won just one of their last six games in all competitions (W1 D3 L2), while Haaland has scored just one goal in his last five appearances, failing to net in each of his last three Premier League matches.

Maresca’s men are winless in four top-flight games and were also held to a 2-2 home draw by Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

After the match, Haaland gave a downbeat interview expressing his frustration, with City’s poor run of form leaving the squad "questioning everything".

"We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want," Haaland told TNT Sports. "Football is easy and difficult.

“When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think, but it's not so easy.

"We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best."

Maresca was then asked to share his thoughts on Haaland’s comments and recent form ahead of Man City’s blockbuster Premier League showdown with champions Arsenal on Sunday.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Maresca said: "I think Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but not just Erling, everyone.

"Remember just a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. You can write and think many different things.

"Erling is upset. I'm upset because we're not winning games. But this is our job, this is football. That's why I need to maintain the balance."

Asked if Haaland’s mood affect his performances, with some social media clips showing him visibly frustrated on the pitch, Maresca replied: "I think he gesticulates when we were winning games, and not receiving balls.

"He's a nine. They live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don't score or win games they're upset. So I don't think that affects his game, but for sure he's not happy not winning games but everyone is on the same page."

Maresca has also insisted that Haaland has been training as normal, adding: "He has been good. Yes, normal like since day one.

“Again, a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch, he was dancing in training. He's happy. It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games, but I don't see any problem at all with Erling."

With Man City sitting six points behind Arsenal at the top of the Premier League table and in danger of falling further behind in the title race, Maresca has made it clear that his team will “try our best” to win at the Emirates Stadium.

Haaland will relish another battle with Arsenal, having scored in six of his previous eight Premier League meetings with the Gunners, netting in each of his last four such games.

The Norwegian should therefore fancy his chances of ending his three-game goal drought in the Premier League; only twice before has he ever gone goalless for four straight matches, and never longer than that.

#1484. Manchester City favourites to sign Borussia Dortmund star after formal approach

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester City are continuing to invest in young talent as they look to strengthen their squad for the future, with another exciting prospect emerging on their transfer radar.

Pep Guardiola’s side have reportedly moved into pole position for one of Borussia Dortmund’s most highly rated youngsters.

United States international Mathis Albert has attracted interest from several European clubs, but City are currently considered the favourites to secure his signature.

With the teenager’s first-team opportunities limited in Germany, the Premier League champions could look to take advantage of the situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester City are the frontrunners to sign Albert after making a formal approach during the summer transfer window.

The report claims City are prepared to offer the 17-year-old lucrative personal terms as they step up their pursuit. Their interest is serious, with the club previously prepared to meet a valuation in the region of €20 million (£16.7m).

Chelsea are also long-term admirers of the youngster and were reportedly willing to spend a similar amount last winter. Paris Saint-Germain previously made contact with Dortmund in 2025, while Arsenal and Liverpool have more recently been monitoring his situation.

However, City are currently viewed as being in the strongest position should Dortmund soften their stance.

Albert joined Borussia Dortmund from the LA Galaxy academy in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of the most exciting young American talents in European football. He has already made Bundesliga appearances and earned senior international recognition with the United States.

Despite his potential, opportunities under Niko Kovac have been limited this season. That lack of regular first-team football has encouraged several clubs to monitor his development, although Dortmund remain determined to keep hold of their young attacker.

The Bundesliga side have reportedly rejected approaches, including loan enquiries, and continue to view Albert as an important part of their long-term plans. They are also preparing a contract extension offer, with his current agreement running until June 2027.

There is another important factor for City. Premier League regulations prevent English clubs from signing Albert permanently until he turns 18 in May, meaning any potential transfer would be geared towards next summer rather than an immediate move.
